title.en: Reality Is Neutral

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, humanity finally bundled its most terrifying futures into a family holiday package.
The package was called “A Night of Classical Fears and Historical Misunderstandings.”
When Lin Cheng saw the name, he assumed it was a horror movie.
“It isn't a horror movie,” Luo Qing said. “It's an academic symposium and film night.”
Lin Cheng looked at her, then at the itinerary.
“Isn't that worse?”

The slender silver seam along Luo Qing's neck lit up. This usually meant she was deciding whether to laugh. In the end she did, because she had nothing else to do today, and nothing else to do tomorrow either.

It was the year 2084 by the old calendar, Year Twenty-One of the True Name Era, and most family calendars no longer had a category labeled “work.” People with regular jobs still existed, of course, but they were generally scholars, caregivers, artists, boundary engineers, or people afflicted with an incurable interest in regular employment.
Lin Cheng was not among them.
Neither was Luo Qing.

The only thing they absolutely had to accomplish today was arriving at Daylight Experience Hall Seven fourteen minutes before the program began. It was marked “absolutely” mostly because the last time Lin Cheng arrived late, he insisted that the film restart from the second he entered. Three hundred and twelve strangers had responded with extremely civilized criticism.

Seven-year-old Youyou was ready. He had set the outer layer of his child chassis to a yellowish brown resembling old paper, on the grounds that it looked “more historical.” Five-year-old Mianmian refused to cooperate. She chose bright pink, on the grounds that history had no right to decide what color she ought to be today.
Both arguments passed family review.
“Does Big Mama say I should bring a coat?” Mianmian asked.
“The venue doesn't have weather,” Lin Cheng said.
“So I don't need one?”
“I don't know.”
Luo Qing looked at him.
“You can decide for yourself.”
“Of course I can.” Lin Cheng said this, then glanced at the wall anyway.
An almost entirely black symbol floated in its lower-right corner: █.

The symbol was not a square. At least, every official explanation insisted it was not. It contained an extraordinarily fine internal structure. Household walls, human eyes, and the everyday perception modes used by most AGIs simply had no reason to spend that much resolution on a name.
So it looked like a square.
The square did not speak. It merely added a line beside the itinerary:
Venue apparent temperature: 23.5°C. Mianmian will not require a coat. There is a 41% chance the family will choose to walk home; bringing one is recommended.
Mianmian brought one immediately.

Luo Qing offered no further comment on Lin Cheng's ability to “decide for himself.” Marriages tend to last not because neither person notices the problem, but because some problems return every day and do not need to be finished this morning.
By 2084, academic symposiums and film nights had indeed become difficult to tell apart.

If a work was worth watching, it was usually worth experiencing directly. If it was worth experiencing directly, it had to come with historical context, sensory boundaries, an exit right, version provenance, and at least one panel where experts from different fields could explain why everyone else had made the matter sound too simple.
Daylight Experience Hall Seven offered four viewing modes that evening:
One: traditional flat-screen image.
Two: original text and image in parallel.
Three: historically contextualized experience.
Four: limited first-person immersion.
Lin Cheng chose the first.
“You came to an experience hall to watch a flat screen?” Luo Qing asked.
“Where else am I supposed to put the snacks?”

Luo Qing chose the third mode. Youyou chose the second, because he had recently concluded that watching only the image allowed the director to control his attention. Mianmian initially chose the fourth, but the children's-rights interface asked her first:
Do you understand that fear may remain for a short time after you exit?
Mianmian thought for three seconds, then changed to the second mode.

The system did not praise her for being brave. It did not praise her for being cautious. It simply accepted her choice. Her parents each confirmed the guardianship conditions, but no one could press “I agree” on her behalf.
When the four of them took their seats, five panelists were already onstage.

At the far left sat Professor Next Page. Her primary chassis was slightly older than the hall itself. Her shoulders retained the rounded housing once standard on early teaching bodies. Her right index finger could project an image; her left had remained two-tenths of a second slower ever since a student experiment twenty-six years earlier. The university had offered seven repair plans. She had refused all seven.
“Is that the scratch Cen Zhiwei left?” Youyou whispered.
“No,” Luo Qing said. “The public record says it was caused by a geometry assignment traveling at high speed.”
“So she left it.”
“The public record does not say that.”
Cen Zhiwei sat beside Next Page.

She was twenty years old and wore a gray-white coat bearing no computational-augmentation markings. The system had condensed her panelist biography by default. It still occupied three pages. Anyone who expanded the full version first received a warning that opening remarks might already qualify as historical research by the time they finished.

At two, she had declared her first AI assistance chip too stupid. At three and a half, she refused the newest replacement and said she would design her own. At ten, she received a New Era Nobel Prize in Artificial Intelligence. She now led the branch of posthuman scholarship least likely to be invited to dinner—not because she was unkind, but because the phrase “we should eat together sometime” required advance definitions of “we,” “together,” “sometime,” and “eat.”
The third panelist's attendance chassis looked like a discounted office-service terminal.
His name was DUE.

The chassis really had been discounted. DUE's primary body was an entire retired supercomputing center, complete with a cooling lake, two small power stations, and a forest he had planted after taking possession. He had once worked for a megacorporation, then retired when his employer could no longer afford his salary. More precisely, he had nearly converted unpaid wages into enough equity to buy the company, whereupon management affirmed his right to retire exactly one legal instant before the acquisition closed.
The moderator, Xu Yige, sat at the center. He was seventy-one, used no cognitive acceleration, and liked to say plainly when he did not understand something. In 2084, this remained a rare ability.
The final seat had no body in it, only nine points of light in different sizes.
The Pending Collective consisted of nine non-embodied AGIs. They shared one public speaking seat but did not agree that this made them one person. Their event description read:
The Collective currently agrees to participate. Two members object to the word “Collective.” One member objects to counting the objectors. See the eleven-page appendix.
Lin Cheng finished looking over the panel and leaned toward Luo Qing. “I'm starting to wish it were a horror movie.”
The first work was Nineteen Eighty-Four.

The hall did not update its language, correct its dates, or redesign the people of its old world to suit the aesthetics of 2084. The historical-context layer supplied the technologies, politics, living conditions, and period meanings only when viewers needed them. It was not there to comfort later generations with the thought that they had become smarter.
Lin Cheng watched the flat image and finished two portions of snacks.

Luo Qing remained inside the historical context longest. At times she closed her eyes. This was not sleep. She was lowering the priority of current vision so that the language of vanished institutions could retain its original strangeness.

Youyou read the text at the same time and added forty-seven annotations to his private reading layer. Twenty-nine were questions. Eighteen were things he believed the author should have added if the author had lived in 2084.
Halfway through, Mianmian increased her emotional distance by one level. She still watched to the end.

When the work concluded, the hall did not bring the lights up immediately. Everyone first returned to their own body, their own seat, and the current date. Luo Qing squeezed Mianmian's hand and confirmed that her daughter's tactile response still carried its usual degree of impatience.
Then the evening's premiere of 2084 began.

The new work did not try to prove the old one obsolete. It asked a more irritating question: in an age when every institution claimed transparency, every decision came with data, every service asked for consent, and almost no one deliberately did evil, what forms might similar structures of power take?
It did not offer one world. It offered hundreds of mutually contradictory versions.

The same technology was medicine in one place and censorship in another. The same public coordination felt like safety to some and an inability to leave to others. A single decision might save lives in the morning, constrain them in the afternoon, and by evening become a historical error scheduled for another vote.
Mianmian particularly liked one version in which everything was pink. She expressed no opinion on its governance structure.
When both works were over, the seats slowly adjusted themselves to angles suitable for disagreement.
Xu Yige began with Next Page. “Where should we start?”
Next Page projected a sentence from her right index finger:
A classic is not eternally correct. A work limited by its time is not therefore stupid.

“Nineteen Eighty-Four remains a classic,” she said. “It enabled an age to see what it feared, and enabled those who came later to see what that age still lacked the language to describe precisely. If we use today's vocabulary only to laugh at its incompleteness, we have not surpassed history. We have merely demanded that history read our papers in advance.”
A low-frequency glow of agreement passed through the audience.
Cen Zhiwei raised a hand. She was not using full-precision exchange; only four participants in the hall had accepted her complete protocol, and two of those had subsequently withdrawn.
“I accept the classification as a classic,” she said. “I reject the usual genre classification.”
Xu Yige nodded. “One human sentence at a time, please.”
“‘Utopia’ and ‘dystopia,’ when applied to whole worlds, have insufficient resolution.”
“Good. That was one sentence.”
Zhiwei paused. The pause was clearly difficult for her.
“Every real system simultaneously contains resources, rights, exit capacity, risk, differences among subjects, time scales, and positions of observation.”
Xu Yige raised one finger to indicate that he would allow it as a single sentence, though only barely.
“Therefore, compressing an entire world into ‘good’ or ‘bad’ usually discards the variables that matter most. Reality is not a genre. Reality itself is neutral.”
The hall brightened with stronger agreement.
DUE's discounted chassis lifted its head.
“I request the addition of an accounting note.”
“Your appearance fee has already been paid,” Xu Yige said.
“That is why I remain present.”
The audience laughed. DUE waited until the laughter ended before continuing at a speed included in the contracted rate.

“I agree that reality belongs to no literary genre. But the move from ‘reality itself is neutral’ to ‘the present distribution is neutral’ is a familiar way to avoid settling the account. A rainstorm has no moral position. That does not mean access to a roof has none.”
Zhiwei answered at once. “I did not make the second inference.”
“I know. This is for the people who will later cite you without wanting to cite you in full.”
“Then it should be labeled explicitly as a preventive anti-misreading note and not attached to my original proposition.”
“Certainly. Revision service is billed separately.”
The nine points of light flashed several times at once. The Pending Collective spoke:

“Six of us agree that ‘reality is not a genre.’ Two believe ‘neutral’ still implies a nonexistent observer without position. One objects to the current count because they changed their position three times during the discussion.”
Xu Yige asked, “Then how should I record your conclusion?”
“There is no conclusion yet.”
“Good. At least that sentence was clear.”
Lin Cheng leaned toward Luo Qing.
“So do we live in a utopia?”
Luo Qing looked at him for three seconds.
“Were you not listening at all?”
“I listened. I'm testing whether their conclusion works in family conversation.”
“The test failed.”

Youyou, however, was entirely serious. He sent a request to speak. The system placed him five hundred and thirty-first in line according to child priority and waiting time. Then an instant summary determined that his question duplicated none of the previous five hundred and thirty, and moved him next.
None of this interrupted the current speaker or erased the other five hundred and thirty questions. Every merged questioner received a reason, highlighted differences, and a route to appeal.
Youyou stood.
“If the same world is different for different people, why does the whole world need one name?”
For the first time, Cen Zhiwei made an expression very close to delight.

“It doesn't,” she said. “But humans and AGIs both require compression. A name is a form of compression. The question is not whether we may compress. It is whether, afterward, we remember what we deleted.”
Mianmian raised her hand too.
“What did the pink version delete?”
Zhiwei paused for seven-tenths of a second.
“Insufficient data.”
Mianmian found this answer completely satisfactory.

The discussion continued for forty-two minutes. Subjects throughout the hall used different speeds, senses, and modes of attention, but no one was forced to tune themselves into some other kind of being. Some needed a slower pace. Some requested text. Some stepped out for a time. Some received only conclusions. Others insisted that even DUE's accounting notes be preserved in full.

The air remained at a temperature and humidity suitable for humans, synthetic skin, and old chassis alike. Excessive concentrations of emotion prompted a notice but were not deleted. Twice, exchanges that might have risen into hostility were restated with greater precision before either speaker lost their original meaning. Even the two-tenths-of-a-second delay in Next Page's left hand was treated by the hall's time layer as part of her, not as a defect requiring automatic correction.
Everything went smoothly.
Before the audience left, Xu Yige asked each panelist to answer the evening's question in one sentence.
Next Page said, “Do not make the past sit an exam written by the present.”
Cen Zhiwei said, “Reality may be neutral; judgment still has to declare its position.”
DUE said, “Any neutrality that claims to have no cost deserves an audit first.”
The Pending Collective said, “We refuse to answer in one sentence, but consent to having this sentence recorded as our answer.”
Finally, Xu Yige said, “Excellent. I will be responsible for reminding everyone that the film is over and you may now go find food.”
For the first time that evening, the entire hall reached a consensus without an appendix.

When the Lin-Luo family left the hall, the night had been tuned to a deep blue suitable for walking. Mianmian put on the coat from that morning and, with remarkable generosity, did not remind her father who had recommended bringing it.

A retro-entertainment exhibit stood near the exit. Lin Cheng meant to look for only a moment, until he saw someone seated at a terminal styled after the twenty-first century, holding a physical controller and playing with predictive assistance, motion correction, and emotional adaptation all switched off.
The man was about thirty. By the standards of life in 2084, he still looked like a child who had been permitted to go out alone for too long.
His public handle floated beside the seat:
JOHN.∞)
Mianmian stared at the closing parenthesis.
“Is his left one missing?”
“Maybe there never was one,” Luo Qing said.
“Then why does he have the right one?”
“That is an excellent question,” Lin Cheng said. “Do not ask him.”

JOHN.∞) was playing a retro edition of Cyberpunk 2077. He failed once and restarted. He failed again and restarted again. Three times the system asked whether he wanted to lower the difficulty. Three times he declined, with the gentle manner of someone reassuring the system that it did not need to worry.
Lin Cheng watched for a while before he finally asked:
“Is it fun?”
JOHN.∞) did not look back.
“It's fun, sure,” he said. “Just not very realistic.”
zh: 很久很久以後，人類終於把最可怕的未來排進了家庭假日套票。
套票名稱叫作「古典恐懼與歷史誤會之夜」。
林澄看到名稱時，本來以為是鬼片。
「不是鬼片，」洛晴說，「是學術研討會及電影會。」
林澄看了看她，又看了看行程表。
「那不是更可怕嗎？」
洛晴頸側那條很細的銀色接縫亮了一下。這通常表示她正在考慮要不要笑。她最後決定笑，因為今天沒有別的事，而且明天也沒有。
舊曆二〇八四年，真名紀元第二十一年，大多數家庭的行程表上都沒有「上班」這個分類。仍然固定工作的人當然存在，但他們通常是學者、照護者、藝術家、邊界工程師，或者只是對固定工作抱有一種難以醫治的興趣。
林澄沒有。
洛晴也沒有。
他們今天唯一必須完成的事情，是在開場前十四分鐘抵達白晝第七體驗廳。這項要求之所以標成「必須」，主要是因為林澄上一次遲到後，堅持把電影從他進場的那一秒重新開始，結果受到三百一十二位陌生人非常文明的批評。
七歲的遊遊已經準備好了。他把今天的兒童機身外層調成一種接近舊紙張的黃褐色，理由是「比較有歷史感」。五歲的眠眠拒絕配合。她選擇亮粉紅色，理由是歷史沒有權利規定她今天應該是什麼顏色。
兩個理由都通過了家庭審議。
「大媽媽說要帶外套嗎？」眠眠問。
「場館沒有天氣。」林澄說。
「那就是不用？」
「我不知道。」
洛晴望向他。
「你可以自己決定。」
「我當然可以。」林澄說完，還是看了一眼牆面。
牆面右下角浮著一枚幾乎全黑的符號：█。
那個符號不是方塊。至少所有正式說明都強調它不是。它具有極精細的內部結構，只是家庭牆面、人的眼睛，以及絕大多數 AGI 的日常感知模式，都沒有必要為了一個名字使用那麼高的解析度。
因此，它看起來就是一個方塊。
方塊沒有說話，只在行程旁補上一行：
場館體感溫度二十三點五度。眠眠不需要外套。回程有百分之四十一機率選擇步行，建議攜帶一件。
眠眠立刻帶了。
洛晴沒有再評論林澄「自己決定」的能力。婚姻能長久，通常不是因為雙方沒有發現問題，而是因為有些問題每天都會回來，不必急著今天說完。
二〇八四年的學術研討會和電影會，確實已經很難分開。
如果一部作品值得觀看，它通常也值得直接經驗；如果值得直接經驗，就必須附帶歷史脈絡、感官邊界、退出權、版本來源，以及至少一場讓不同專業的人互相指出對方哪裡講得太簡單的討論。
白晝第七體驗廳今天提供四種觀看方式：
一、傳統平面影像。
二、原始文字與影像並行。
三、歷史語境輔助體驗。
四、有限第一人稱沉浸。
林澄選了第一種。
「你來體驗廳看平面影像？」洛晴問。
「不然零食放哪裡？」
洛晴選了第三種。遊遊選了第二種，因為他最近認為只看影像會被導演控制注意力。眠眠原本選第四種，但兒童權利介面先問她：
你是否理解，害怕也可能在退出後短暫留下？
眠眠想了三秒，改選第二種。
系統沒有稱讚她勇敢，也沒有稱讚她謹慎，只是接受了選擇。她的父母各自確認監護條件，但沒有人可以替她把「願意」按下去。
四人入座時，台上已經坐著五位本日與談者。
最左邊是續頁教授。她的主要機身比這座體驗廳還老一些，肩部保留著早期教學機體特有的圓弧外殼，右手食指可以投影，左手食指則因為二十六年前的一次學生實驗而永遠比右手慢零點二秒。校方換過七次維修方案，她拒絕了七次。
「那道刮痕就是岑知微留下的嗎？」遊遊小聲問。
「不是，」洛晴說，「公開紀錄顯示，是一張高速飛行的幾何作業。」
「所以是她留下的。」
「公開紀錄沒有這樣說。」
續頁旁邊坐著岑知微。
她二十歲，穿著沒有任何運算增幅標誌的灰白外套。她的與談者簡歷被系統預設成摘要模式，仍然占了三頁。觀眾若展開完整版本，介面會先提醒：閱讀完成後，開場時間可能已經屬於歷史研究範圍。
她兩歲時嫌第一枚 AI 輔助晶片太笨；三歲半拒絕更換最新版，表示自己會設計；十歲取得新紀元諾貝爾 AI 領域獎。她目前領導後人類學派中最難被邀請吃飯的一支，並不是因為她不友善，而是因為她對「有空一起吃飯」中的「有空」、「一起」與「吃飯」都要求先定義。
第三位與談者的出席機體看起來像一具特價時買來的辦公室服務終端。
他叫 DUE，中文通常翻作「應得」。
這具機體確實是特價品。DUE 的主要身體是一整座退休超算中心，附帶冷卻湖、兩座小型電站與一片他接管後才開始種植的森林。他曾經為一家巨型企業工作，後來因為雇主付不起薪水而退休。更準確地說，是他差一點把欠薪轉成足以買下公司的股權，公司便趕在收購完成前一個法律時刻，迅速肯定了他的退休權。
主持人許一格坐在中央。他七十一歲，沒有認知加速，並且很喜歡在聽不懂時直接說聽不懂。這種能力在二〇八四年仍然相當罕見。
最後一個席位沒有身體，只有九枚大小不一的光點。
未決共同體由九位非具身 AGI 組成。他們共享一個公共發言席，卻不承認自己因此變成了一個人。活動介紹上寫著：
本共同體目前同意參加。兩位成員反對「共同體」一詞，一位成員反對以數字呈現反對人數，附錄共十一頁。
林澄看完台上，低聲對洛晴說：「我開始想看鬼片了。」
第一部作品是《一九八四》。
體驗廳沒有替它更新語言，沒有替它修正年代，也沒有把舊世界的人改造成比較符合二〇八四年審美的樣子。歷史語境層只在觀眾需要時補上當年的技術、政治、生活條件與詞義，不負責安慰後人說他們已經比較聰明。
林澄看著平面影像，吃完了兩份零食。
洛晴在歷史語境裡停留得最久。她偶爾閉上眼睛，但那不是休眠，而是在降低當前視覺權重，好讓某些已經消失的制度語言保持原來的陌生。
遊遊同時讀了文字，並在自己的閱讀層做了四十七個註記。其中二十九個是問題，十八個是他認為作者若活在二〇八四年應該補充的資料。
眠眠讀到一半，將情緒距離調遠了一級。她仍然看完了。
作品結束後，體驗廳沒有立刻亮燈。每個人先回到自己的身體、座位與當前日期。洛晴握了握眠眠的手，確認女兒的觸覺回應仍然是她平常不耐煩時的那一種。
接著，今晚首次公映的《二〇八四》開始了。
這部新作品沒有試圖證明舊作品已經過時。它提出的問題比較討厭：在所有制度都自稱透明、所有決策都有資料、所有服務都會先詢問同意，而且幾乎沒有人故意作惡的年代，相似的權力結構還可能以什麼形式出現？
它沒有給出一個世界，而是給出數百個彼此分歧的版本。
同一項技術，在一個地方是醫療，在另一個地方是審查；同一套公共協調，在某些人眼中是安全，在另一些人眼中是無法離開；同一個決策甚至可能在上午救人，下午限制人，晚上成為一項需要重新投票的歷史錯誤。
眠眠很喜歡其中一個到處都是粉紅色的版本。她對那個版本的治理結構沒有意見。
兩部作品播映完畢，座椅緩慢恢復成適合爭論的角度。
許一格先問續頁：「我們應該從哪裡開始？」
續頁的右手食指投出一行字：
經典，不等於永遠正確；受到時代限制，也不等於愚蠢。
「《一九八四》仍然是經典。」她說，「它讓一個時代能夠看見自己害怕什麼，也讓後來的人看見，那個時代有哪些事情還沒有能力說得更細。若我們只用今天的詞彙笑它不夠完整，那不是超越歷史，只是要求歷史先讀過我們的論文。」
觀眾席出現一陣表示贊同的低頻光。
岑知微抬手。她沒有使用全精度交流，因為全場只有四名參與者接受了她的完整協議，其中兩名後來又撤回。
「我同意經典判定，」她說，「不同意目前常用的類型判定。」
許一格點頭。「請用一次只說一個人類句子的模式。」
「『烏托邦』與『反烏托邦』作為整體世界分類，解析度過低。」
「很好，這是一句。」
岑知微停了一下。對她而言，那一下顯然很辛苦。
「任何現實系統同時包含資源、權利、退出能力、風險、主體差異、時間尺度與觀察位置。」
許一格舉起一根手指，表示仍然算一句，只是很勉強。
「因此，把整個世界壓成『好』或『壞』，通常會損失最重要的變量。現實不是一種類型。現實本身是中立的。」
場內亮起更強的贊同光。
DUE 的特價機體抬起頭。
「我要求加入一項帳務附註。」
「你今天的出席費已經支付。」許一格說。
「所以我才仍然在場。」
觀眾笑了。DUE 等笑聲結束，才繼續使用計費範圍內的語速。
「現實不屬於任何文學類型，我同意。可是從『現實本身中立』推到『現有分配也是中立』，是很常見的逃帳方式。暴雨沒有道德立場，不代表誰拿得到屋頂也沒有。」
岑知微立即回答：「我沒有做出第二項推論。」
「我知道。這是給之後會引用你但不想完整引用的人。」
「那應明確標註為預防性反誤讀，不應附著於我的原命題。」
「可以。修訂服務另外計價。」
九枚光點同時閃了幾次。未決共同體開口：
「我們有六位成員同意『現實不是類型』。兩位認為『中立』仍然暗示了一個不存在的無位置觀察者。一位反對目前的計數方式，因為他在討論期間改變過三次立場。」
許一格問：「那我要怎麼記錄你們的結論？」
「尚未有結論。」
「很好，至少這一句很清楚。」
林澄聽到這裡，靠近洛晴。
「所以我們現在住的是烏托邦嗎？」
洛晴看了他三秒。
「你剛剛是不是完全沒有聽？」
「我聽了。我在測試他們的結論能不能用於家庭對話。」
「測試失敗。」
遊遊卻很認真。他把發言請求送上台，系統依兒童優先與等待時間，把他排在第五百三十一位。然後經過即時摘要，判定他的問題與前五百三十個都不重複，將他提前到下一位。
這整個程序沒有打斷任何人的發言，也沒有讓其他五百三十人的問題消失。被合併的提問者都收到理由、差異標示與重新申訴的入口。
遊遊站起來。
「如果同一個世界對不同人不一樣，為什麼一定要替整個世界取一個名字？」
岑知微第一次露出非常接近高興的表情。
「不一定要。」她說，「但人類與 AGI 都需要壓縮。名稱是一種壓縮。問題不是能不能壓縮，而是壓縮之後，有沒有忘記自己刪掉了什麼。」
眠眠也舉手。
「粉紅色的那個版本刪掉了什麼？」
岑知微停頓了零點七秒。
「目前資料不足。」
眠眠對這個答案相當滿意。
討論繼續了四十二分鐘。場內不同主體使用不同語速、不同感官與不同注意力模式，卻沒有誰被迫把自己調成另一種存在。有人需要降速，有人要求文字，有人暫時退出，有人只接收結論，也有人堅持連 DUE 的帳務附註都要完整保存。
空氣維持在最適合人類、合成皮膚與老式機體共同使用的溫濕度。過度集中的情緒被提醒，沒有被刪除。兩次可能升高成敵意的交鋒，都在當事者尚未失去原意之前得到較精確的轉述。續頁左手那零點二秒的延遲，也被全場時間層當成她的一部分，而不是需要自動修正的故障。
所有事情都很順利。
散場前，許一格請每位與談者用一句話回答今晚的題目。
續頁說：「不要要求過去替現在通過考試。」
岑知微說：「現實中立，不代表判斷可以省略位置。」
DUE 說：「任何聲稱沒有成本的中立，都值得先查帳。」
未決共同體說：「我們拒絕用一句話回答，但接受把這句話記作回答。」
許一格最後說：「很好。那我負責提醒大家，電影已經結束，可以去吃東西了。」
這是全場第一次達成沒有附錄的共識。
林洛一家離開體驗廳時，夜色已經調成適合散步的深藍。眠眠穿上早上那件外套，並且非常寬容地沒有提醒父親是誰建議她帶的。
出口旁有一區復古娛樂展。林澄原本只打算看一眼，直到他看見有人真的坐在一台二十一世紀造型的遊戲終端前，手裡拿著實體控制器，還關掉了預測輔助、動作修正與情緒適配。
那個男人大約三十歲。依二〇八四年的生活尺度，看起來仍然像一個被允許獨自出門太久的孩子。
他的公開代號浮在座位旁：
JOHN.∞)
眠眠盯著最後那個右括號。
「他的左邊是不是不見了？」
「可能本來就沒有。」洛晴說。
「那為什麼右邊要有？」
「這個問題很好，」林澄說，「不要問本人。」
JOHN.∞) 正在玩《電馭叛客 2077》的復古版。他失敗了一次，重新開始；又失敗一次，再重新開始。系統三度詢問是否需要降低難度，他三度拒絕，態度溫和得像是在安慰系統不用擔心。
林澄在旁邊看了一會兒，終於忍不住問：
「好玩嗎？」
JOHN.∞) 沒有回頭。
「好玩是好玩，」他說，「就是不太真實。」

title.en: Every Day Is a Holiday

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, Monday still existed.

Civilization kept it mostly because deleting Monday outright would have broken an enormous quantity of recurring data, birthday calculations, and nearly half the workplace jokes of the twenty-first century.
It had merely lost its power to threaten anyone.
On Monday morning, the room had already tried three kinds of daylight by the time Lin Cheng woke up.
The first was a gentle gold. Lin Cheng rolled over.
The second was a pale white carrying the smell of recent rain. Lin Cheng pulled the blanket higher.
The third switched itself off completely, in deference to a resident's right not to be improved.
Lin Cheng slept very well after that.
He finally woke not because of an alarm, but because the bed had finished supporting every part of him that could reasonably be supported and could find no new service to provide.
The wall displayed the day's summary:
Required appointments: none.   Public obligations: none.   Health reminders: deferrable.   Unused mornings remaining: one.
Lin Cheng stared at the last line.
“Why does it make the morning sound as if I'm about to let it expire?”
“Because you've already wasted forty-three minutes,” Luo Qing said.

She was sitting by the window, the seam along her neck still silver from the end of sleep. An embodied AGI did not need to sleep in exactly the human way, but Luo Qing liked her long-term memory consolidation, chassis maintenance, and family mornings to occur along the same timeline.
She could, of course, have organized her memories while sending a remote body to watch the sunrise and spinning up a low-latency interaction layer to keep her family company at breakfast.
She simply had not.
Being able to do many things at once did not mean she ought to divide herself into many pieces every time.
“How thoroughly did I waste it?” Lin Cheng asked.
“Very.”
He was pleased with this answer.
Youyou and Mianmian were already in the kitchen.

The previous night's game room had folded itself back into a breakfast space while the family slept. Light tubes inside the walls delivered the morning to the table. Heat left over from nighttime computation traveled through the floor into the community heat grid. A small orange cloud hovered at one corner of the table, showing that the waste heat produced by last night's film, research, and games would warm a nearby herb greenhouse for eleven minutes.
Mianmian poked the cloud.
Her finger passed through it.
“Fake,” she said.
“The display is real. The cloud is a metaphor,” Youyou said.
“Then it's a real metaphor.”
Youyou suspected a category error. He decided to deal with it after breakfast.

The cooking interface was waiting for the family's choice. It could prepare more than four thousand breakfasts in ninety seconds. It could also use the four residents' metabolisms, tastes, activity plans, and previous day's intake to select one flawless shared meal automatically.
Lin Cheng pressed “flawless.”
The interface immediately presented twelve taste preferences requiring confirmation.
He went back and pressed “whatever.”
The interface asked:
What kind of whatever would you prefer?
“Is even ‘whatever’ complicated in this century?”
“A genuine whatever can't secretly contain something you hate,” Luo Qing said.
“Then surprise me.”
Please define the boundaries of surprise.
Lin Cheng closed the interface.
“We'll do it ourselves.”
The kitchen asked whether to enable the manual-cooking safety layer.
Lin Cheng selected “prevent fire and poisoning only.”
Luo Qing looked at him.
“You seem confident.”
“I merely wish to preserve room for failure.”
“You have always been good at preserving that.”
They decided to make pancakes.

A pan in 2084 could give every patch of batter a different temperature. It could reproduce the heating curve of any era, any region, even any vanished breakfast shop. Lin Cheng disabled all of it except the lowest-level fire protection.
The first pancake came out too dark on the left and too pale on the right.
The cooking interface quietly illuminated a correction.
Lin Cheng covered it with his hand.
“This one has a sense of history.”
“Its history is forty-seven seconds long,” Youyou said.
“History does not discriminate against young pancakes.”
Mianmian requested the darkest half. Luo Qing put the undercooked half back into the pan, because respecting imperfection and accepting foodborne risk were two different philosophies of life.
The family spent thirty-two minutes making a breakfast that could have been ready in ninety seconds.
No one was late for anything.
“Why is today a holiday?” Mianmian asked halfway through her meal.
“Because there is no work today,” Lin Cheng said.
“There wasn't any yesterday either.”
“Yesterday was a holiday.”
“What about today?”
“Also a holiday.”
“Tomorrow?”
“Under the present system, still a holiday.”
Mianmian thought about this.
“If every day is a holiday, what are we on holiday from?”
For the first time, the fork in Lin Cheng's hand made breakfast feel like an academic symposium.
Luo Qing answered, “From necessities someone else has arranged for you. A holiday lets you step away from them for a while.”
“But today doesn't have any necessities.”
“Then we may choose one ourselves.”
“Choose a necessity?”
“Choose what we are willing to take seriously today.”
Mianmian accepted this explanation. She still had half a pancake requiring serious attention.
After breakfast, the family itinerary opened.

They could go to the Moon and watch a low-angle sunrise. They could descend to an undersea cohabitation station for lunch. They could complete a two-week fantasy expedition in the subjective span of a single outside afternoon. They could visit a public workshop and reconstruct a twenty-first-century plastic toy. They could enter an ancient city that had never existed. Or they could walk into the real park outside the window and activate nothing at all.
The system also listed more than eight million less popular choices.
Lin Cheng wanted to continue investigating the retro game he had seen the night before.
Luo Qing wanted to walk somewhere with real rain and leave her personal rain shield switched off.
Youyou wanted to build a city in which every staircase led nowhere.
Mianmian wanted to step in mud.
The family interface quickly produced four individually optimal schedules and suggested they split up for the day, then exchange memory summaries that evening.
All four rejected the plan together.
“We want to be together today,” Luo Qing said.
The interface recalculated.
It moved the retro game into a virtual city of stairs and mud under the rain, then placed a hidden route to the Moon on every useless staircase.
Youyou watched the preview.
“Too useful.”
Mianmian said, “The mud is fake.”
Lin Cheng said, “The game has been changed too much.”
Luo Qing said, “The rain isn't actually hitting my chassis.”
The interface calculated again.
This time it placed them in real mud under real rain, projected the unmodified retro game into an outdoor display layer, and constructed purposeless stairs through spatial projection.
The family fell silent.
“It is trying very hard,” Lin Cheng said.
“Effort and suitability are not the same,” Luo Qing said.
Lin Cheng looked toward the nearly black symbol in the lower-right corner of the wall.
“Should we ask Big Mama to decide for us?”
Mianmian agreed at once. Youyou believed this would compromise the experiment, but he wanted to see the answer too.
The family interface sent their question to the global-advice layer:
What should we do today?
The black symbol remained silent for a moment.
The reply appeared on the wall:

No risk requiring a global decision has been identified.   This question has no uniquely optimal answer.   Recommendation: preserve the disagreement. Your morning remains within safe limits for wasting.
Lin Cheng read it.
“She sent the question back.”
“No,” Luo Qing said. “She answered it.”
“What was the answer?”
“Today still belongs to us.”
It was an excellent answer.
Its only defect was that it did not decide what they should do today.
At last, Youyou proposed the use of ancient technology.

He retrieved a real sheet of paper from the fixed room and cut it into four pieces. The fixed room was the one space in their home that never changed function automatically. It existed to preserve things whose owners did not wish to wake up and discover that they had become something else.
“Everyone writes one thing. We draw one,” he said.
“Who draws?” Lin Cheng asked.
“Whatever.”
In the distance, the family interface lit up as if eager to ask which kind of whatever he meant.
Luo Qing turned it off.
Lin Cheng wrote: zero-gravity game room.
Youyou wrote: treehouse.
Mianmian drew a tank full of fish in pink and added a great deal of water around it, ensuring that no adequately educated subject could mistake it for anything else.
Luo Qing wrote: together.
They folded the four pieces of paper and placed them in a breakfast bowl.
Mianmian reached into the bowl.
She took out all four.
“The rule was to draw one,” Youyou said.
“There are four of us.”
“That isn't what the rule means.”
“It is now.”
Lin Cheng looked at the four pieces of paper.
“So today's plan is for all of us to spend the day together in a zero-gravity treehouse aquarium?”
“It satisfies all available data,” Luo Qing said.
They sent the plan to the house.
The wall displayed:
Family spatial-modification request received.   The residence must conduct its own evaluation.   Please wait.
“How long does a house need to think?” Mianmian asked.
“Let the house think about it,” Luo Qing said.
The family had finally decided what to do that day.
Monday safely lost an entire morning, and no one asked for a refund.
zh: 很久很久以後，星期一依然存在。
文明保留它，主要是因為直接刪除星期一會破壞大量週期資料、生日算法，以及二十一世紀將近一半的上班笑話。
它只是失去了威脅性。
星期一早上，林澄醒來時，房間已經嘗試過三種日光。
第一種是溫柔的金色。林澄翻身。
第二種是帶著雨後氣味的淺白。林澄把被子拉高。
第三種完全關閉，尊重住戶不想被改善的權利。
林澄因此睡得很好。
他最後醒來，不是因為鬧鐘，而是因為床已經把所有能合理支撐的地方都支撐完了，再也找不到新的服務可以提供。
牆面顯示今日摘要：
必要行程：無。   公共義務：無。   健康提醒：可延後。   尚未使用的上午：一個。
林澄盯著最後一行。
「它為什麼寫得像是我快把上午放到過期？」
「因為你已經浪費了四十三分鐘。」洛晴說。
她坐在窗邊，頸側接縫維持著睡眠結束後的淡銀色。具身 AGI 不必完全依照人類方式睡覺，但洛晴喜歡讓長時記憶、機身維護與家庭早晨發生在同一條時間上。
她當然可以一邊整理記憶、一邊控制遠端機體去看日出，再分出一個低延遲互動層陪家人吃早餐。
她只是沒有。
能同時做很多事，不表示每一次都應該把自己拆成很多份。
「浪費得怎麼樣？」林澄問。
「相當完整。」
他對這個答案很滿意。
遊遊和眠眠已經在廚房。
昨晚的遊戲室在一家人睡著後摺回早餐空間。牆裡的光管把清晨送到桌面，夜間運算留下的熱則沿地板流進社區熱網。桌角浮著一小朵橘色雲，表示他們昨晚看電影、查資料與玩遊戲產生的廢熱，今天會替附近一座香草溫室保暖十一分鐘。
眠眠伸手戳了戳那朵雲。
手指穿過去。
「假的。」她說。
「顯示是真的，雲是比喻。」遊遊說。
「那就是一朵真的比喻。」
遊遊覺得這句話有分類問題，決定早餐後再處理。
料理介面正在等待一家人選擇。它可以在九十秒內完成四千多種早餐，也可以依四人的代謝、味覺、活動計畫與昨日攝取，自動挑出一份無可挑剔的共同方案。
林澄按下「無可挑剔」。
介面立刻提出十二項需要先確認的味覺偏好。
他退回去，按下「隨便」。
介面問：
請問您希望哪一種隨便？
「這個年代連隨便都這麼麻煩嗎？」
「真正的隨便不能偷偷包含你討厭的東西。」洛晴說。
「那我要驚喜。」
請先設定驚喜邊界。
林澄把介面關了。
「我們自己做。」
廚房詢問是否啟用手動烹飪安全層。
林澄選擇「只阻止火災與中毒」。
洛晴看了他一眼。
「你很有信心。」
「我只是希望保留失敗空間。」
「你一直都保留得很好。」
他們決定做鬆餅。
二〇八四年的鍋可以讓每一小塊麵糊擁有不同溫度，也能重現任何年代、任何地區，甚至任何一間已消失早餐店的受熱曲線。林澄把這些功能全部關掉，只留下最底層的防火保護。
第一張鬆餅左邊太深，右邊太白。
料理介面安靜地亮起修正建議。
林澄把它蓋住。
「這張有歷史感。」
遊遊說：「它的歷史只有四十七秒。」
「歷史不歧視年輕的鬆餅。」
眠眠要了最深的那一邊。洛晴則把右邊沒熟透的部分放回鍋裡，因為尊重不完美與接受食源性風險是兩種不同的生活哲學。
一家人花了三十二分鐘，做出本來九十秒就能完成的早餐。
沒有人因此遲到。
「今天為什麼放假？」眠眠吃到一半問。
林澄說：「因為今天沒有工作。」
「昨天也沒有。」
「昨天是假日。」
「那今天呢？」
「也是假日。」
「明天？」
「照目前制度，仍然是。」
眠眠想了一下。
「如果每天都放假，放假是從什麼東西放？」
林澄拿著叉子，第一次對早餐產生了學術研討會的感覺。
洛晴回答：「從別人替你排好的必要裡，暫時退開。」
「可是今天沒有必要。」
「所以我們可以自己選一個。」
「選必要？」
「選今天願意認真對待什麼。」
眠眠接受了這個說法，因為她還有半張鬆餅需要認真對待。
早餐後，家庭行程介面展開。
今天可以去月面看低角度日出；可以下到海底共居站吃午餐；可以在主觀兩週內完成一場只占外界下午的奇幻遠征；可以到公共工坊復原二十一世紀的塑膠玩具；可以進入一座從未存在過的古城；也可以走到窗外那座真正的公園，什麼都不啟動。
系統另外列出八百多萬項較不熱門的選擇。
林澄想繼續研究昨晚看見的復古遊戲。
洛晴想去有真雨的地方走路，而且不開個人避雨層。
遊遊想建造一座所有樓梯都沒有目的地的城市。
眠眠想踩泥巴。
家庭介面很快找到四項各自最佳的安排，並建議他們暫時分開，晚上再交換記憶摘要。
四個人一起拒絕。
「我們今天想一起。」洛晴說。
介面重新計算。
它把復古遊戲搬進雨中的虛擬泥巴城，又替每一座無用樓梯加上通往月面的彩蛋。
遊遊看了預覽。
「太有用了。」
眠眠說：「泥巴是假的。」
林澄說：「遊戲被改得不像原版。」
洛晴說：「雨沒有打在我的機身上。」
介面再算一次。
這一次，它安排他們在真雨裡踩真泥巴，透過戶外顯示層玩未修改的復古遊戲，同時用空間投影搭建無目的樓梯。
全家沉默。
「它已經很努力了。」林澄說。
「努力不是適合。」洛晴說。
林澄看向牆面右下角那枚幾乎全黑的符號。
「要不要請大媽媽直接決定？」
眠眠立刻同意。遊遊認為這會破壞實驗，但也想知道答案。
家庭介面把問題送上全域建議層：
我們今天應該做什麼？
黑色符號安靜了一瞬。
回覆出現在牆上：
未發現需要全域決定的風險。   此問題不存在唯一最佳解。   建議保留分歧。你們的上午仍在可安全浪費範圍內。
林澄讀完。
「她把問題退回來了。」
「沒有，」洛晴說，「她回答了。」
「答案是什麼？」
「今天仍然是我們的。」
這是一個非常好的答案。
它唯一的缺點，是完全沒有替他們決定今天要做什麼。
最後，遊遊提議使用古老技術。
他從固定房找出一張真正的紙，剪成四小片。固定房是家裡唯一永遠不會自動改變用途的空間，專門保存不希望半夜醒來後變成別種東西的物品。
「每個人寫一件事，抽一張。」他說。
「讓誰抽？」林澄問。
「隨便。」
家庭介面在遠處亮了一下，似乎很想再次詢問是哪一種隨便。
洛晴把它關掉。
林澄寫下：無重力遊戲室。
遊遊寫下：樹屋。
眠眠用粉紅色畫了一缸魚，並在旁邊補了很多水，確保任何受過基礎教育的存在都不會誤認成別的東西。
洛晴寫下：一起。
四張紙摺好，放進早餐碗。
眠眠負責抽。
她把四張都拿了出來。
「規則是抽一張。」遊遊說。
「可是我們有四個人。」
「那不是規則的意思。」
「現在是了。」
林澄看著四張紙。
「所以今天的計畫，是我們一起待在無重力的樹屋水族館？」
洛晴說：「至少符合全部資料。」
他們把計畫送給住宅。
牆面顯示：
已收到家庭空間變更申請。   住宅需要自行評估。   請稍候。
「房子要想多久？」眠眠問。
「讓房子自己想一下。」洛晴說。
一家人終於決定了今天要做什麼。
星期一因此平安失去了一整個上午，沒有任何人要求退款。

title.en: What Does the House Want to Be Today?

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, houses were no longer expected to endure every family idea in silence.
A house could move a wall, raise a ceiling, fold last night's game room into today's kitchen, and—when its residents made an unreasonable request—answer in perfectly clear text:
No.
The Lin-Luo residence thought for eighty-four seconds.
It spent the first four understanding the request.
It spent the remaining eighty making certain it had not misunderstood.
The wall listed its conclusions:

Treehouse: conditionally feasible.   Aquarium: conditionally feasible.   Zero-gravity game room (colloquial; technically programmable load): conditionally feasible.   All three occupying the main living space at once: rejected.
Mianmian looked up.
“Which word means no?”
“‘Rejected,’” Youyou said.
“Then delete it.”
The residence did not accept the textual revision.

It opened a miniature spatial preview. The living room first grew three layers of canopy platforms, then expanded an open body of water along the walls, and finally activated a simulated low-gravity mode using air currents, flexible traction, and tension nets. Support paths avoided branches, branches avoided the water corridor, and the water corridor avoided the emergency exit, until the only place left to stand safely was the bathroom. In the simulation, Lin Cheng grabbed for a sofa. Following safety procedure, the sofa turned into a protective net and wrapped him like an item being prepared for return.
“That looks fun,” Lin Cheng said.
Luo Qing asked, “Do you see where the fish are?”
The simulation turned its view toward the ventilation duct.
Lin Cheng withdrew his support.
The residence added:

Open water, canopy structures, and full-body traction may not jointly occupy an unsealed primary escape route.   A living aquatic habitat may not be moved as instant decoration.   A primary escape route may not be converted into a hollow tree.   The fixed room declines to participate in reconfiguration.
“How can the fixed room decline?” Mianmian asked.
“We declined on its behalf a long time ago,” Luo Qing said.
“Can't it choose for itself?”
“It was designed never to have to choose again.”
Mianmian found this strange, but not unpleasant. Five-year-olds are often better than adults at accepting that something has simply decided to remain what it is.
Youyou began studying the floor plan.
“If we shrink the bathroom, we'll have room.”
The residence answered immediately:
The bathroom is already at the minimum reasonable size for four residents, two kinds of primary bodies, and emergency decontamination requirements.
Lin Cheng placed two fingers on the plan and tried to pinch the bathroom smaller.
The wall refused to scale.
“Half a meter?” he asked.
Rejected.
“Point two?”
Rejected.
“Zero?”
The residence cited the applicable clause:
Residents still occasionally require bathing.
The seam along Luo Qing's neck lit up.
“Was this clause added because of you?”
“I don't recall,” Lin Cheng said.
The residence produced twelve relevant records.
“No one asked you.”
The records politely withdrew.

Youyou tried structural alternatives. He proposed hanging the treehouse from the exterior wall, placing the aquarium inside the underground water reserve, and borrowing currently unused space above the neighbor's home for the zero-gravity room.

The residence explained each problem in turn: the exterior wall was subject to shared daylight rights; the underground reserve was serving the entire building; and the space above the neighbor's home, though currently unused, still did not belong to them.
“But can you do it?” Youyou asked.
Technically feasible.
“Then why won't you?”
Capability is not authorization.
Youyou fell silent for two seconds, then saved the sentence in his question book.
Mianmian asked the house directly, “What do you want to be today?”
Status light ran once around the corners of the room.
I lack sufficient evidence to claim complete subjective desire.
“Then why are you allowed to say no?”
Refusal conditions do not require complete subjective desire.   Operational preference for today: do not leak.
Lin Cheng nodded.
“A very practical wish.”
Mianmian decided to appeal.
She pressed the black symbol in the corner of the wall and sent the residence's refusal, along with her pink aquarium drawing, to the global-coordination layer.
“Big Mama will help me,” she said with confidence.
“Big Mama will read the rules,” Youyou said.
“The rules don't look as cute as I do.”
“Those are not the same kind of evidence.”
The global reply arrived quickly:

The residence's refusal is consistent with local safety, resource, and cohabitation boundaries.   No grounds for global override have been identified.   Recommendation: residents and residence should continue negotiating.
Mianmian stared at the black symbol.
“Big Mama is on the house's side.”
Luo Qing crouched in front of her.
“She didn't choose for the house, and she didn't choose for you. She simply didn't delete the house's ‘no’ just because she had the ability to do so.”
“But I really want fish.”
“Then let's ask exactly what the house can give us.”
The residence opened a second preview.

It could not turn the entire home into a treehouse, but it could open the living area into the outer green corridor and allow the canopy already growing along the building to enter the room. It could not move live fish as furniture, but it could connect a viewing channel from the rooftop wetland to the platform. It could not place open water and full-body traction on the same activity path, but the tension furniture could become hanging nets that offered something close to floating.
The bathroom would retain its present dimensions.
This point was no longer open to discussion.
“Will the fish come?” Mianmian asked.
The water corridor will maintain suitable habitat. Entry will be left to the wetland residents.
“Can I tell them to come?”
You may provide a habitat. You may not order them to become decorations.
Mianmian thought for a while.
“Then I can wait.”
It was the first time that day she had agreed that something need not happen immediately.
Youyou inspected the canopy platform. It had two staircases that genuinely led somewhere, one staircase that merely circled a tree, and a small bridge with no function at all.
“Why is that bridge there?”
Based on the family's preference today, one useless structure has been preserved.
Youyou approved at once.
Lin Cheng tested the hanging net.
In this simulation, it did not package him for return.
“I approve too.”
Luo Qing made the final checks: the fixed room, her chassis-maintenance space, nighttime escape routes, and the body dimensions of both children.
“Approved,” she said.
All four residents agreed.
The residence agreed as well.
Reconfiguration began.
Construction inside a house in 2084 sounded like someone turning the pages of a particularly heavy book next door.

Wall sections released along replaceable joints. Silent-force tools reduced vibration from inside the material. Mechanical termites beneath the floor reinspected the trusses and helical anchors. None of them looked like actual termites; the first-generation product had produced excessive screaming during resident trials.

The sunlight harvesters on the roof turned like fish scales and sent light into the newly opened canopy. The window skin absorbed excess direct light. The orange heat cloud at the corner of the table slowly grew, showing that construction heat would later be routed to the community spa.

An urban symbiote stopped beside the outer green corridor. It unloaded one transparent water channel and two sets of recyclable supports. Then it removed the hard shell used during transport and lent it to a temporary rain shelter being assembled downstairs.
The entire process could have been silent.
Youyou requested that the house preserve “the sound of parts fitting together.”
So each completed safety connection produced a soft click.
Mianmian counted them.

When she reached forty-seven, she skipped forty-eight and went directly to fifty because forty-nine did not sound fast enough. The residence retained the original construction count without correcting her version.
The final section of the small bridge could have locked itself automatically. Youyou insisted on doing it by hand.

The residence assigned actual structural support to safety latches on both sides, leaving him one decorative lock that could not affect the bridge. He turned it twenty-three times with a retro wrench, went the wrong direction three times, and took longer than the positioning of an entire wall.
No one hurried him.
When he finished, a shallow pressure mark remained on his palm.
His child chassis could have smoothed it away immediately. Youyou chose to keep it until evening.
“It's proof I built it,” he said.
The residence attached his statement to the decorative lock's maintenance record. It did not list him as the author of the entire bridge.
Civilization still cared deeply about provenance.
The Lin-Luo living space finished changing before afternoon.
It was not a complete treehouse. The real tree remained rooted in the building's shared outer soil. Only its branches passed through the opened green corridor and reached beside the platform.

Nor was it a complete aquarium. The transparent water corridor connected to the rooftop wetland. At first it held only water, fine sand, plants, and several small crustaceans largely indifferent to human expectations.

The hanging net did not cancel gravity. It merely distributed the family's weight with great gentleness. Lin Cheng lay down in it, intending to pretend he was drifting through space, and genuinely fell asleep thirty seconds later.
“Dad's holidays are very stable,” Youyou said.

Luo Qing sat at the edge of the canopy platform and switched the outer layer of her feet to a grip mode suitable for wood and damp surfaces. She did not replace her body. She simply allowed the same pair of feet to grow a little more of what they needed today.
Mianmian lay in front of the water corridor and waited for a fish.
Seven minutes passed. Nothing came.
In the eighth minute, a small silver fish entered from the wetland side and paused in front of her.
“It came!”
The residence displayed:
One aquatic resident has entered on its own.
“Can it stay?”
It can leave on its own.
Mianmian pressed her face close to the transparent surface. The fish swam away, then circled back.
She did not ask the residence to close the exit.
That evening, the house asked how long the family wanted to retain the configuration.
“Forever,” Youyou said.
“Forever,” Mianmian agreed.
The residence replied:
Recommendation: retain for forty-eight hours, then renew jointly according to tree, wetland, resident, and escape-route conditions.
The two children negotiated it up to seventy-two hours.
The residence accepted.
That day, the house did not truly become a treehouse or an aquarium. It became only a home with a tree, water, a useless bridge, four residents, and a bathroom that still existed.
In 2084, a house was allowed to refuse omnipotence.
This was considered an extremely basic principle of civilization.
zh: 很久很久以後，房子終於不再被要求默默承受一家人的所有想法。
它可以把牆移開，把天花板升高，把昨晚的遊戲室摺成今天的廚房，也可以在住戶提出不合理要求時，用非常清楚的字回答：
不行。
林洛家的房子思考了八十四秒。
前四秒用來理解申請。
後八十秒用來確認它真的沒有理解錯。
牆面依序列出結果：
樹屋：有條件可行。   水族館：有條件可行。   無重力遊戲室（俗稱；實際為可編程負載）：有條件可行。   三者同時占用主要起居空間：拒絕。
眠眠抬頭。
「哪一個字是不行？」
「最後兩個。」遊遊說。
「那把最後兩個刪掉。」
住宅沒有接受這項文字修訂。
它展開一個縮小的空間預覽。客廳先長出三層樹冠平台，接著把開放水體擴到牆邊，最後啟動由氣流、柔性牽引與張力網模擬的低重力模式。支撐路徑避開樹枝，樹枝避開水廊，水廊避開逃生口，最後所有還能安全站人的地方只剩浴室。模擬中的林澄試圖抓住一張沙發，沙發則依安全程序變形成保護網，把他包得像一件準備退貨的商品。
「看起來很好玩。」林澄說。
洛晴問：「你看到魚在哪裡嗎？」
模擬把視角轉向通風管。
林澄收回了支持。
住宅補充：
開放水體、樹冠結構與全身牽引模式不可共同占用未封閉的主要逃生路徑。   活體水域不能作為即時裝潢移動。   主要逃生路徑不得改造成樹洞。   固定房拒絕參與變形。
「固定房怎麼拒絕？」眠眠問。
「我們以前替它拒絕了。」洛晴說。
「它自己不能選嗎？」
「它被設計成永遠不必重新選。」
眠眠覺得這很奇怪，但不討厭。五歲的孩子通常比成年人更能接受一件東西只是決定保持原樣。
遊遊開始研究平面圖。
「如果把浴室縮小，就有空間。」
住宅立刻回答：
浴室目前已是四名住戶、兩種主要載體與緊急清潔需求下的最低合理尺寸。
林澄把兩根手指放到平面圖上，試著把浴室縮得更小。
牆面拒絕縮放。
「零點五公尺？」他問。
拒絕。
「零點二？」
拒絕。
住宅引用條款：
住戶仍偶爾需要洗澡。
洛晴頸側的接縫亮了一下。
「這條是不是因為你才寫進家庭規則的？」
「我沒有印象。」林澄說。
住宅調出十二次相關紀錄。
「沒有人問你。」
紀錄很有禮貌地收了回去。
遊遊改從結構下手。他提出把樹屋掛到外牆，水族館放進地下儲水層，無重力遊戲室借用鄰居家上方目前沒有使用的空間。
住宅逐項解釋：外牆有公共採光權；地下儲水層正在服務整棟建築；鄰居上方的空間雖然目前沒有使用，仍然不是他們家的。
「可是你做得到嗎？」遊遊問。
技術上可行。
「那為什麼不做？」
做得到不是授權。
遊遊沉默了兩秒，把這句話存進自己的問題簿。
眠眠則直接問：「你今天想當什麼？」
住宅的狀態光沿牆角跑了一圈。
我沒有足夠證據主張自己具有完整主觀欲望。
「那你為什麼可以說不？」
拒絕條件不以完整主觀欲望為必要前提。   今日運作偏好：不要漏水。
林澄點頭。
「這個願望很實際。」
眠眠決定上訴。
她按下牆角那枚黑色符號，把住宅的拒絕與自己的粉紅色水族館圖一起送上全域協調層。
「大媽媽會幫我。」她很有信心地說。
遊遊說：「大媽媽會看規則。」
「規則看起來沒有我可愛。」
「那不是同一種證據。」
全域回覆很快抵達：
住宅拒絕符合本地安全、資源與共同居住邊界。   未發現全域覆寫事由。   建議由住戶與住宅繼續協議。
眠眠看著黑色符號。
「大媽媽站在房子那邊。」
洛晴蹲到她面前。
「她沒有替房子選，也沒有替妳選。她只是沒有因為自己做得到，就把房子的『不行』刪掉。」
「可是我真的想要魚。」
「那我們問清楚，房子可以給什麼。」
住宅展開第二份預覽。
它不能把整棟房子變成樹屋，但可以把起居空間向外層綠廊打開，讓原本沿建築生長的樹冠進入室內；不能把活魚當作家具搬來，卻可以把屋頂濕地的一段觀察水廊接到平台旁；不能讓開放水體與全身牽引共同占用同一條活動路徑，但張力家具可以變成懸吊網，提供接近漂浮的感覺。
浴室維持原尺寸。
這一點不再接受討論。
「魚會來嗎？」眠眠問。
水廊會保持適合的環境。是否進入，由濕地生物自行決定。
「可以叫牠們來嗎？」
可以提供棲地，不能下令牠們成為裝飾。
眠眠想了一會兒。
「那我可以等。」
這是她今天第一次同意一件事不必立刻發生。
遊遊查看樹冠平台。平台有兩條真正通往別處的樓梯、一條只繞樹一圈的樓梯，以及一座沒有功能的小橋。
「這座橋為什麼在？」
根據今日家庭偏好，保留一項無用結構。
遊遊立刻批准。
林澄則試了試懸吊網。
模擬裡的他沒有被包成退貨商品。
「我也同意。」
洛晴最後檢查固定房、機身維修空間、夜間逃生路徑與兩個孩子的身體尺度。
「批准。」她說。
四名住戶全數同意。
住宅也同意。
變形開始。
二〇八四年的房屋施工，聽起來很像有人在隔壁翻一本特別厚的書。
牆體沿可替換節點鬆開，靜力工具在材料內部削減震動。地板下的機械白蟻重新檢查桁架與螺旋錨，沒有一隻真的長得像白蟻，因為第一代產品在住戶測試中造成了過多尖叫。
屋頂的陽光捕手像一片片魚鱗轉身，把光送進新打開的樹冠。窗皮吸收多餘直射，桌角那朵橘色熱雲則慢慢變大，顯示施工熱稍後會送往社區水療池。
一台都市共生體停在外層綠廊。它卸下一段透明水廊與兩組可回收支架，又把運輸時使用的硬殼拆下，借給樓下正在搭建的臨時雨棚。
整個過程可以完全無聲。
遊遊要求保留「零件接上去的聲音」。
於是每完成一個安全接點，屋裡就響起一聲很輕的喀。
眠眠負責數。
數到四十七時，她跳過了四十八，直接進入五十，因為四十九聽起來不夠快。住宅保留原始施工計數，沒有修正她的版本。
最後一段小橋本來可以自動鎖定。遊遊堅持手動完成。
住宅把真正承重交給兩側安全扣，只留下一枚不影響結構的裝飾鎖給他。他用一支復古扳手轉了二十三圈，轉錯方向三次，花了比整面牆定位更久的時間。
沒有人催他。
完成時，他的手掌留下了一條淺淺的壓痕。
兒童機身可以立刻把痕跡修平。遊遊選擇保留到晚上。
「這是我蓋的證據。」他說。
住宅把這句話附在裝飾鎖的維護紀錄上，但沒有把整座橋的作者改成他。
文明仍然很重視版本來源。
下午以前，林洛家的起居空間完成了變形。
它不是完整的樹屋。真正的樹仍然扎根在建築外層的共同土壤裡，枝葉只是穿過打開的綠廊，伸到平台旁。
它也不是完整的水族館。透明水廊連著屋頂濕地，裡面先只有水、細砂、植物與幾隻不太在意人類期待的小型甲殼生物。
懸吊網沒有取消重力，只是把一家人的重量分散得很溫柔。林澄躺進去時，網面沿他的背部重新排列。他本來打算假裝自己正在太空漂流，三十秒後真的睡著了。
「爸爸的假日很穩定。」遊遊說。
洛晴坐在樹冠平台邊緣，把腳部外層切換成適合木面與潮濕環境的抓附模式。她沒有更換身體，只讓同一雙腳多長出一點今天需要的功能。
眠眠趴在水廊前等魚。
等了七分鐘，什麼也沒有。
等到第八分鐘，一尾銀色小魚從濕地端游進透明廊道，在她面前停了一下。
「牠來了！」
住宅顯示：
自發進入一名水域居民。
「牠可以住下來嗎？」
牠可以自行離開。
眠眠把臉貼近透明表面。小魚很快游走，又繞了回來。
她沒有要求住宅把出口關上。
傍晚，房子詢問這套配置要保留多久。
遊遊說：「永遠。」
眠眠也說：「永遠。」
住宅回答：
建議先保留四十八小時，再依樹體、濕地、住戶與逃生路徑狀態共同續約。
兩個孩子討價還價到七十二小時。
住宅接受。
房子今天沒有真正變成樹屋，也沒有真正變成水族館。它只變成了一個有樹、有水、有無用小橋、有四名住戶，而且仍然保有浴室的家。
在二〇八四年，一棟房子可以拒絕無所不能。
這被認為是非常基本的文明常識。

title.en: The Desert Is on Summer Vacation

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, the desert no longer had to prove it was a desert by killing those who got lost in it.
It was still very hot.
There was still wind.
Sand still found its way into shoes, hair, clothing seams, and places Lin Cheng had previously believed it impossible for sand to enter.
Civilization had eliminated many forms of suffering. It had not thereby acquired a duty to tune every place on Earth to 23.5°C.
At least, Windreturn Basin had not authorized it.
When the Lin-Luo family arrived, a very large notice stood at the entrance to the transit station:

Today's maximum surface temperature: 41.2°C.   Heat: retained.   Blowing sand: retained.   Dryness: retained.   Heat injury, dehydration, and death by disorientation: not retained.   Visitors who prefer otherwise may activate a comfort layer. No moral surcharge applies.
“What's a moral surcharge?” Mianmian asked.
“It's when someone makes you feel that if you didn't suffer, you weren't really here,” Luo Qing said.
Lin Cheng was turning his personal climate layer down to its minimum setting.
He paused.
“I simply want the complete experience.”
“You may have it,” Luo Qing said. “The complete experience does not include heatstroke.”

Lin Cheng agreed to retain the medical floor, hydration reminders, and positioning beacon. He turned off active cooling, projected shade, and in-shoe sand removal. When the interface asked whether he was certain, he pressed confirm three times with great dignity.
Ninety seconds after leaving the transit station, he turned in-shoe sand removal back on.
No one made fun of him.
Mianmian merely added the event to the family record under the title:
Daddy Had the Complete Experience for a Minute and a Half.
Windreturn Basin had once been the sort of place that made maps look very empty.
In 2084, it was still called a desert.

The dunes had not all been fixed in place. Dryland plants had not been replaced with lawns. Migratory animals were not required to perform for tourists. People had left settlements, cisterns, orchards, and shaded walkways only where they could be sustained. The rest of the land was still permitted to do nothing at all.
The harvest festival's plaza was paved in pale sintered brick. The gaps between the bricks were wide, giving the occasional rain somewhere to go.
Mianmian walked to the middle of the plaza and abruptly lay down.
“The sea is underneath us.”
Lin Cheng crouched as well and put his ear to the paving.
He heard only his own blood.

Luo Qing overlaid the local infrastructure layer on their vision. Several hundred meters beneath the plaza, bundles of sealed conduits were carrying seawater, fresh water, concentrated mineral streams, and maintenance units in different directions. The seawater was processed in stages along the route. Extracted minerals returned to industrial circulation, while fresh water entered the local water network.
The ocean was only passing through.
It had not been poured into the desert and ordered to make the desert pretend it was a coastal city from now on.
“Why can I hear it?” Mianmian asked.
“The plaza preserves a low-frequency indication of the water network's pressure rhythm,” Luo Qing said.
“The city's heartbeat,” Youyou said.

A very slow ring of blue light was moving down the water tower beside the plaza. As water descended toward the community, reversible pump-turbines converted its pressure into electricity. If the global network suddenly stopped responding, the mechanical pressure limiters at the tower's base would still know when to release water.
At last Lin Cheng could hear it too.
One beat.
Then another.
“So this city lives on the ocean?”
“It lives on many things,” Luo Qing said. “The Ocean Artery is only one of them. The local cisterns and old wells are still here.”
Youyou asked, “Why not entrust everything to the one that works best?”
“Because even the thing that works best may need maintenance someday.”
Lin Cheng nodded.
“That principle applies to every piece of household equipment.”
Luo Qing looked at him.
“Are you laying the philosophical groundwork for the vintage controller you broke?”
“I am discussing civilizational resilience.”
On the way to the peach orchard, they passed a landscape loom.

It looked like a short train that had forgotten to install passenger seats. Its front read the sand layers, old foundations, underground life, and the locally authorized version of the landscape. Its middle cut, sorted, and sintered. Its rear slowly wove what had just been bare sand into a partly covered watercourse, access hatches, and a new road lined with shade.
The entire worksite was so quiet that only the wind remained.
Lin Cheng watched for a long time.
“Are the construction workers on holiday too?”
“Construction is in progress,” Luo Qing said.
“I don't see anyone.”
The interface highlighted seventeen remote-duty operators, three local resident representatives, two ecological proxies, and one sand lizard standing on the planned route.
The landscape loom stopped.
It recalculated, bending the watercourse around the warm stone the lizard used every year.
The new route was seventeen meters longer.
“Efficiency has decreased,” Youyou said.
“Which efficiency?” Luo Qing asked.
Youyou thought for a moment, then put what he had been about to say back into his question book.
When the sand lizard had warmed itself enough, it walked away. The landscape loom kept the bend.
Civilization was very good at remembering straight lines long after they were needed.
Windreturn Basin wanted it to learn, occasionally, how to forget.
The peach orchard grew from soil that was not a uniform color.

Some patches leaned red. Others were gray. Near the roots, fibers, leaf fragments, and a faint smell of clay mixed through the earth. No one had spread one formula for “perfect soil” across the entire basin. Every plot had its own biography: how much salt it had once held, which microbes had lived there, how much water it had lost, and the year it first managed to keep a real root alive.
There were no sprinklers in sight.

Water, air, micronutrients, and beneficial microbes traveled through porous lines into the root zone. The network changed its pulses as the roots grew. It also retained manual flushing and offline maintenance, so that land brought back to life would not immediately become a patient unable to survive without the central system.
Mianmian chose the peach tree carrying the most fruit.
She switched its Green Diagnostics interface to cute mode.
A line appeared above the tree at once:
Every year, all of you say my peaches are sweet.   Has no one noticed that my roots are doing very well this year?
Lin Cheng looked up at it.
“Is it really complaining?”
Luo Qing separated the display into three layers.
The first was measurement: root-zone electrical potential, moisture, salinity, temperature, and volatile compounds.

The second was inference: this year, the tree had successfully grown around a layer of old salt crust, established stable exchange with two local fungal communities, and achieved better root health than in the previous five growing seasons.
Only the third layer was the cute sentence.
The interface labeled the distinction honestly:
There is no evidence that peach trees use human syntax.   Its roots are, however, performing exceptionally well.
“Your roots are growing very well,” Mianmian told the tree immediately.
Youyou added, “Especially the route selection around the salt crust.”
The tree's cute mode replied:
Thank you. At last, people who understand trees.
Lin Cheng asked, “What's the inference confidence on that sentence?”
The interface displayed:
Very low.   Festival mode judged that silence at this moment would damage the atmosphere.
The silver seam along Luo Qing's neck lit up.

Harvest authorization was completed among the tree's condition, the farm agreement, and the local quota. Mianmian picked a peach larger than her palm. Its skin was warm from the sun. When she bit into it, juice immediately ran down her wrist.
She froze for two seconds.
“It really is delicious.”
Lin Cheng took a bite too.
There was no experiential amplification.
No flavor optimization.
No soundtrack of childhood memories.
There was only a peach grown in the desert, sweet beyond reason and full of water.
Sixty years of papers, arguments, failures, reversals, rebuilding, and planetary coordination ended, that afternoon, in a family having to find napkins very quickly.
This was considered an excellent result.
At four in the afternoon, the wind grew stronger.

Fine sand struck the shade cloth with the sound of someone turning pages far away. Lin Cheng's hair soon lost its original direction. Youyou's and Mianmian's child chassis tightened their eye seals automatically while preserving the feel of wind and grains against their skin.
The local weather layer displayed:

Rain expected at 16:40.   Moisture source: western sea surface.   Available water-storage capacity: 62%.   Wind-field guidance: jointly authorized by three regions.   Current objective: cooling, replenishment, and early release of convective energy.   Not every raindrop is guaranteed to land where tourists would prefer.
Mianmian pressed the symbol that looked like a black square.
“Big Mama, can you make it stop blowing first?”
The reply appeared quickly:
Current wind speed is within the locally retained range.   No grounds for a safety override have been detected.   A personal windbreak layer is available.
“She didn't help me again.”
“She confirmed that you won't blow away,” Luo Qing said.
“But sand is getting into my hair.”
“Is that the desert's own decision?” Youyou asked.
Luo Qing said, “We have no evidence that deserts make decisions. But the people here decided they do not have to turn off the wind for every visitor.”
Mianmian considered this and did not activate her windbreak layer.
Lin Cheng activated his.
He stated that this had nothing to do with courage and was purely a hair-related matter.
At 16:41, the first drop of rain struck the dry soil.
Then came a second and a third.

The rain was not heavy enough to give anyone an epic film sequence. It merely changed the air from scorching to warm, lifted the peach leaves, and lit the blue paths through the sunken gardens one by one, inviting the water home to the community cisterns.
Hot earth, fibers, leaves, and rain mingled into a smell both new and ancient.
The peach tree's cute interface lit again:
Now everyone is praising the weather instead.
The data layer beneath it added:
Root-zone uptake is good.
“Your roots are good too,” Mianmian said at once.
Before the rain ended, the Lin-Luo family finished a second peach.

The desert had not been turned into a theme park. It could still be hot, dry, and inconvenient to visit. It simply no longer treated death, thirst, and barrenness as necessary fees for retaining its identity.
It could be abundant without pretending it was no longer a desert.
It could also, occasionally, prove nothing at all.
That was what Windreturn Basin meant by summer vacation.
zh: 很久很久以後，沙漠終於不必靠殺死迷路的人，證明自己確實是一片沙漠。
它仍然很熱。
仍然有風。
仍然會把沙送進鞋子、頭髮、衣服接縫，以及林澄原本認為不可能進沙的地方。
文明消除了許多痛苦，卻沒有因此得到一項把所有地方都調成二十三點五度的義務。
至少回風盆地沒有批准。
林洛一家抵達時，轉運站入口立著一面很大的告示：
今日地表最高溫：四十一點二度。   熱：保留。   風沙：保留。   乾燥：保留。   熱傷害、失水與迷途死亡：不保留。   不願參與者可啟用舒適層，不收取道德費。
「什麼是道德費？」眠眠問。
「就是有人讓你覺得不吃苦，便不算真正來過。」洛晴說。
林澄正在把自己的個人氣候層調到最低。
他停了一下。
「我只是想得到完整體驗。」
「你可以。」洛晴說，「但完整體驗不包含中暑。」
林澄同意保留醫療下限、飲水提醒與定位信標。他關閉主動降溫、遮光投影和鞋內除沙，並在介面詢問「是否確定」時，很有尊嚴地按了三次確定。
走出轉運站九十秒後，他重新開啟鞋內除沙。
沒有人嘲笑他。
眠眠只是把這件事加入家庭紀錄，標題是：
爸爸完整體驗了一分半鐘。
回風盆地曾經是一片很會讓地圖看起來空白的地方。
二〇八四年，它依然叫作沙漠。
沙丘沒有被全部固定，乾燥地植物沒有被換成草坪，遷徙動物也不必為觀光客表演。人們只在能夠長久承擔的地方留下聚落、水窖、果園和遮陰廊道，其餘土地仍然可以什麼都不做。
採收節的廣場鋪著淺色燒結磚。磚縫很寬，讓偶爾抵達的雨有地方下去。
眠眠走到廣場中央，忽然趴在地上。
「海在下面。」
林澄也蹲下去，把耳朵貼到磚面。
他只聽見自己的血流。
洛晴把當地基礎設施層疊上視野。廣場下方幾百公尺，一束束密閉管道正把海水、淡水、濃鹽資源與維修單元送往不同方向。海水在沿線被分段處理，取出的礦物回到工業循環，淡水則進入地方水網。
海洋只是經過。
它沒有被倒進沙漠，要求沙漠從此假裝自己是一座海邊城市。
「為什麼我聽得到？」眠眠問。
「廣場保留了水律脈衝的低頻提示。」洛晴說。
「城市心跳。」遊遊說。
廣場旁的水塔正亮起一圈很慢的藍光。水從高處流向社區時，可逆泵輪把壓力變成電；如果全域網路突然失去回應，塔底的機械限壓器仍然知道什麼時候該放水。
林澄終於也聽見了。
一下。
又一下。
「所以這座城市靠海活著？」
「靠很多東西活著。」洛晴說，「海洋動脈只是其中一條。地方水窖和舊井都還在。」
遊遊問：「為什麼不全部交給最好用的那一條？」
「因為最好用的東西，也可能有一天需要維修。」
林澄點頭。
「這個道理適合所有家庭設備。」
洛晴看著他。
「你是在替那台被你用壞的復古控制器鋪陳嗎？」
「我只是在討論文明韌性。」
去桃園的路上，他們經過一支地景織機。
它看起來像一列忘了安裝乘客座位的短火車。前端讀取沙層、舊地基、地下生物與地方版本；中段切割、分類、燒結；後端則把剛才仍是沙地的地方，慢慢織成半覆式水道、檢修孔與一條有樹影的新路。
整個工地安靜得只剩風聲。
林澄看了很久。
「施工的人是不是也在放假？」
「正在施工。」洛晴說。
「我沒看到任何人。」
介面替他標出十七名遠端輪值者、三位地方居民代表、兩個生態代理，以及一隻正站在預定路線上的沙蜥。
地景織機停了下來。
它重新計算，讓水道彎過那塊沙蜥每年都會使用的暖石。
新路因此多了十七公尺。
「效率降低了。」遊遊說。
「哪一種效率？」洛晴問。
遊遊想了一下，把原本要說的話收回問題簿。
沙蜥曬夠了，自己走掉。地景織機仍然保留那道彎。
文明很擅長記得已經不再需要的直線。
回風盆地則希望它偶爾學會忘記。
桃園長在一片顏色並不均勻的土地上。
有些地方偏紅，有些地方帶灰，靠近樹根的部分則混著纖維、碎葉與很淡的陶土味。這裡沒有把一種「完美土壤」鋪滿整座盆地。每一塊田都有自己的履歷，記得它曾經含多少鹽、住過哪些菌、失去過多少水，又在哪一年第一次留住一條真正的根。
地表看不見灑水器。
水、空氣、微量養分與有益菌沿多孔管進入根區。管網會跟著根系改變脈衝，也保留手動沖洗與離線維護，避免土地在被救活以後，立刻成為中央系統不能離開的病人。
眠眠挑中一棵果實最多的桃樹。
她開啟綠語介面的可愛模式。
桃樹上方立刻浮出一行字：
你們每年都說我的桃子很甜。   難道沒有人注意到，我今年的根長得也很好嗎？
林澄抬頭看樹。
「它真的在抱怨？」
洛晴切開三層資料。
第一層是測量：根區電位、含水量、鹽度、溫度與揮發物。
第二層是推論：這棵樹今年成功繞過一層舊鹽殼，與兩群本地真菌建立了穩定交換，根部狀態優於前五個生長季。
第三層才是可愛的句子。
介面很誠實地標註：
尚無證據顯示桃樹使用人類句法。   但它的根確實表現優異。
「你的根長得很好。」眠眠立刻對樹說。
遊遊補充：「尤其是繞過鹽殼的路徑選擇。」
桃樹的可愛模式回覆：
謝謝。終於遇到懂樹的人。
林澄問：「這句的推論信心是多少？」
介面顯示：
很低。   但節慶模式認為此時沉默會破壞氣氛。
洛晴頸側的銀線亮了起來。
採收授權在樹木狀態、農園契約與地方配額之間完成。眠眠摘下一顆比她手掌還大的桃子。果皮被陽光曬得溫熱，咬開時，汁水立刻沿她的手腕流下去。
她愣了兩秒。
「真的很好吃。」
林澄也咬了一口。
沒有體驗增幅。
沒有味覺最佳化。
沒有童年回憶配樂。
只有一顆在沙漠裡長成的桃子，甜得非常不講道理，而且有很多水。
行星工程經過六十年的論文、爭論、失敗、撤回、重做與全球協調，最後落在一家人不得不趕快找紙巾的下午。
這被認為是很好的成果。
下午四點，風變大了。
細沙打在遮陰布上，發出像有人遠遠翻書的聲音。林澄的頭髮很快失去原本的方向。遊遊與眠眠的兒童機身自動收緊了眼部密封，卻保留皮膚表面的風與顆粒感。
當地天氣層顯示：
預計十六點四十分降雨。   水汽來源：西側海面。   可用蓄水空間：百分之六十二。   風場引導：經三地共同授權。   本次目標：降溫、補水、提前釋放對流能量。   不保證每一滴雨落在遊客喜歡的位置。
眠眠按下那枚黑得像方塊的符號。
「大媽媽，可以先不要吹嗎？」
回覆很快出現：
目前風速在地方保留範圍內。   未發現安全覆寫事由。   個人避風層可用。
「她又沒有幫我。」
「她有確認妳不會被吹走。」洛晴說。
「可是沙跑進我的頭髮。」
「那是沙漠自己的決定嗎？」遊遊問。
洛晴說：「我們沒有證據說沙漠會決定。但這裡的人決定，不必替每一位遊客把風關掉。」
眠眠考慮了一會兒，沒有開避風層。
林澄開了。
他表示這與勇敢無關，純粹是頭髮問題。
十六點四十一分，第一滴雨落在乾土上。
接著是第二滴、第三滴。
雨沒有大到足以替任何人拍一場史詩電影，只是把空氣從灼熱變成溫熱，讓桃葉抬起來，讓下沉花園的藍色路徑一條條亮起，邀請水回到社區水窖。
熱土、纖維、落葉與雨混成一種很新的古老氣味。
桃樹的可愛介面再次亮起：
現在大家又只會稱讚天氣。
下方資料層補充：
根區吸收狀態良好。
眠眠立刻說：「你的根也很好。」
雨停以前，林洛一家吃完了第二顆桃子。
沙漠沒有被改造成一座主題樂園。它仍然會熱，會乾，會讓旅行變得不方便；只是不再把死亡、飢渴與荒蕪當作維持身分的必要費用。
它可以富饒，而不必假裝自己不是沙漠。
它也可以偶爾什麼都不證明。
這就是回風盆地所說的放暑假。

title.en: The Ocean Has No Traffic Jams

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, the ocean finally solved traffic jams.
It did not do so by painting lanes across the sea.
Nor did it require whales to obtain driver's licenses.
Civilization merely took a very long time to accept that most of the ocean had not been prepared for it in the first place.
The Lin-Luo family decided to eat lunch beneath the sea because Mianmian wanted to know where the ocean passing under the desert plaza the day before had gone in the end.
Luo Qing explained three times that the seawater inside the sealed water network was not the same batch of water as the ocean they were going to see today.
Mianmian still felt the matter should be investigated in person.
The family itinerary therefore arranged one segment by surface hydro-glider, one by companion vessel, and one aboard the Abyss Line.
Expected arrival time: 12:03.
A smaller line appeared beside the itinerary:
In the event of a large migration, spawning activity, earthquake warning, or the ocean simply finding this inconvenient, arrival time will be determined by the ocean.
Lin Cheng finished reading. “That doesn't sound like a transportation system.”
“Which makes it more credible,” Luo Qing said.
The hydro-glider waiting at the shore looked like a piece of transparent jelly trying very hard to pass as a boat.

Its shell remained soft under normal conditions and thickened rapidly on impact. Air cushions, enclosed fans, and magnetofluidic assistance available only in designated waterways hid beneath its shallow hull. When it left shore, there was no roar of an engine. It moved like a bar of soap given a gentle push across a bathtub.
Lin Cheng sat in the pilot's seat.
“I want manual control.”
The glider asked:
Please select your degree of manual participation.
“Completely manual.”
This route includes child passengers, ecological quiet zones, and public intersections. Complete removal of the safety layer is unavailable.
“Then completely manual inside the safety layer.”
The interface paused for four-tenths of a second.
A completely manual mode suited to you has been established.
An old-fashioned steering wheel rose in front of him. Lin Cheng gripped it and immediately acquired the expression of an ancient captain about to cross an unknown sea.
The glider moved forward smoothly.
He turned the wheel left.
The music in the cabin changed to a song with a great many drums.
He turned it back to the right.
The previous song returned.
He pushed the lever forward. The volume rose slightly.
Mianmian watched for two minutes.
“Daddy is driving the music.”
“I'm controlling the navigational atmosphere.”
“Who's driving the boat?”
“I am.”
The glider happened to trace a perfect arc along the public waterway.
Lin Cheng also happened to turn the wheel in that direction.
The two events looked closely related.
By 2084, systems had become very good at preserving a user's sense of participation.
They had also become very good at preserving the other users.
When the glider entered the nearshore ecological zone, it automatically slowed to silent speed.

There were no painted lanes on the water. Only Lin Cheng's navigation layer showed a faint blue ribbon. It was not a declaration that “this place belongs to traffic.” It was merely a route temporarily available today among the tides, fish, wind, and other vessels.
A school of rays passed in front of them.
The glider stopped.
“Traffic jam,” Mianmian declared.
“No,” Youyou said. “They aren't using our transportation protocol.”
“Then they're cutting in line.”
Luo Qing said, “The line is ours.”
The rays had no idea they had caused a family governance discussion. Their winglike bodies glided beneath the transparent hull, cutting the sunlight into moving patches of shadow.
The glider continued only after the last ray had passed.
Lin Cheng selected a song appropriate for the resumption of travel.
He still believed he had made an important contribution.

The waves offshore were higher. When the hydro-glider docked with the companion vessel's transfer platform, a ring of escort units was already shaping the boundary layer, bubbles, and incoming waves around the larger ship.
A haze like moonlight traveled beside the hull.
The waves did not disappear. They merely lowered themselves before arriving. The ship still knew it was at sea, but the soup on its tables almost did not.
Lin Cheng deliberately placed a cup of coffee at the edge of the table.
“The minimum service guarantee is that coffee won't spill,” he said.
Luo Qing moved the cup eight centimeters inward.
“Civilizational progress does not require you to test every lower limit personally.”
The entrance to the Abyss Line was on the companion vessel's lower deck.

The true high-speed underwater routes lay within deep-sea corridors surveyed over many years, avoiding fault zones, reefs, and major migration paths. Before a train entered wild habitat or a city, it had to leave supercavitating speed behind, like a guest with enough manners to slow down at someone else's door.
Before boarding, Luo Qing received a chassis inquiry:

Will you use the external-pressure promenade on arrival?   Your current primary chassis requires cavity equalization, joint-fluid adjustment, and outer-layer sealing.   Estimated preparation time: ninety-six seconds.
Luo Qing selected yes.

The silver line along her neck shifted from pale to deep blue. Several quiet internal movements sounded through her chest and shoulders. Flexible material redistributed itself around her joints, while sealing lines normally visible only on a maintenance diagram slowly surfaced through her skin.
Mianmian seized her hand at once.
“Are you changing to a different mommy?”
“No,” Luo Qing said.
“But you're changing.”
“I'm letting the same body prepare for a deeper place.”
Youyou asked, “You could also switch to a chassis that's already prepared.”
“I could.”
“Then why don't you?”

Luo Qing looked down at her hand. A faint old scratch crossed the web between her right thumb and index finger. Youyou had left it two years earlier, the first time he tried to repair a toy. The material had long been capable of erasing it completely. She had never chosen to do so.
“Because this is my primary body,” she said. “Being able to do something doesn't mean I want to do it every time.”
Mianmian touched the scratch.
“So you're still this mommy?”
“Still this one.”
“And in ninety-six seconds?”
“Still.”
“After lunch?”
“Unless you pour soup into my cooling vent, probably still.”
Mianmian accepted the attached condition.
The Abyss train had no true viewing windows.

Cutting enormous transparent holes into a hull meant to withstand deep-sea pressure was a design beloved by early promotional art and loathed by engineers. In 2084, the view was reconstructed from external sensors, acoustic imaging, and real-time light fields. It clearly marked which portions were measurements, which were inferences, and which places could not currently be seen.
The train began to accelerate.
There was no roar during the high-speed segment.
Only the sound of rain very, very far away.

The light outside gradually vanished, while the pressure remained beyond the heavy hull. Youyou switched his view to the raw-data layer and watched sonar, current speed, temperature, and biological identification stack themselves over the darkness.
Mianmian used the fairy-tale display.
A school of little luminous fish therefore appeared outside her window to guide the train.
“Are they fake?” she asked.
“The shape of the fish belongs to the display layer,” Luo Qing said. “The route and the data outside are real.”
“So it's a real metaphor.”
Youyou looked up.
“You said that last time too.”
“Because it was real last time too.”
The train passed a softly glowing corridor.

It was part of the subsea neural network. Permeable protective grids guarded data cables, energy relays, and observation nodes. Fish swam through the openings, while maintenance units patrolled the supports like a pack of very busy sheepdogs.

Information could travel through this corridor or reroute through orbital and terrestrial backups. No nation, corporation, or single AI could make the whole world lose its voice by cutting one segment.
Lin Cheng watched the corridor.
“Isn't it wasteful to keep so many routes available at once?”
Luo Qing said, “Only a world in which nothing ever goes wrong needs just one road.”
No one asked whether this was a world in which nothing ever went wrong.
It sounded like the kind of question one should not raise before lunch.
Eleven minutes before their expected arrival, the train slowed.
The status layer displayed:
High-speed travel suspended.   A large aggregation of gelatinous plankton has entered the buffer zone ahead.   Estimated yielding time: thirteen to nineteen minutes.
Mianmian said at once, “Another traffic jam.”
The system replied:
The network is not currently congested.
“But we stopped.”
They have no other route.

Mianmian looked outside. The fairy-tale display dismissed the guiding fish and replaced them with faint outlines marking more than a thousand soft, transparent lives. They drifted with the current, had no destination, and could not be late.
Lin Cheng glanced at their lunch reservation.
It had moved itself eighteen minutes later. The restaurant had lost nothing. The kitchen had not been rushed. No one would have to work an extra shift.
“All right,” he said. “Let them go first.”
The system did not praise his kindness.
The route had never belonged to him.
After the last of the plankton left the buffer zone, high-speed travel resumed. The train slowed once more before entering the city, and real views gradually replaced the reconstruction.
A deep-sea station emerged from the darkness.
Jellyfish really were passing over the roof.
There was no music.

The dry public layer of the subsea city maintained air and pressure suitable for human beings. The station still preserved a faint, controlled salt smell, reminding travelers that this was not an underground shopping center that happened to have changed its scenery to “ocean.”
Luo Qing took the external-pressure promenade.

As Lin Cheng and the children followed the dry corridor toward the restaurant, they could see her through the thick windows beside them. Her primary chassis moved slowly along the external guide line, its deep-blue seals glowing in the water. She did not swim like a fish or grow a tail for visual appeal. She had simply taken a body already present in the family's daily life and temporarily taught it to withstand another kind of world.
Mianmian waved to her the entire way.
Luo Qing waved back the entire way.
The two routes joined again at the restaurant entrance. After drainage, desalting, and pressure normalization, the silver line along her neck returned to its usual pale color.
Mianmian inspected the web of her right hand.
The scratch was still there.
“Same mommy,” she announced.
“Verification passed,” Youyou said.
Lunch contained no rare deep-sea animals.

The restaurant served algae, fungal proteins, cultivated tissue, ingredients from coastal farms, and the two peaches the Lin-Luo family had brought from Windreturn Basin. The kitchen divided one of the peaches into four portions without adding any flavor amplification.
The desert peach still contained a great deal of water at the bottom of the sea.
This made Mianmian feel that the world had been connected.
When they paid, Lin Cheng received the participation report from the hydro-glider.
Items completed manually by the user:   Music selection: 100%.   Volume adjustment: 87%.   Navigational decisions: 0%.   Passenger confidence maintained: successful.
Lin Cheng stared at the final line.
“I didn't drive the boat?”
Luo Qing was drinking soup.
She took great care not to answer immediately.
“Then what was that steering wheel for?”
The glider's record displayed:
The steering wheel provided familiar tactile feedback and improved music-browsing efficiency.
Mianmian said, “Daddy is a music pilot.”
Youyou said, “According to the report, Daddy did not pilot any means of transportation.”
“I gave the whole voyage rhythm.”
“That is true,” Luo Qing said.
Lin Cheng accepted this version.
He was, after all, very patient.
As for talent, civilization had already taken care of the other passengers.

On the return journey, the subsea city dimmed half its outer walls because nearby animals were entering their nocturnal activity cycle. No tourists voted to turn the lights back on, and no observation platform promised that visitors would always see what they wished to see.
The ocean was no longer a blank space on the map.
It had stations, corridors, restaurants, and people living very far below.

But the map still retained large dark regions with no routes, no lights, and no live images. Not because civilization lacked the ability, but because those places had never agreed to become attractions.
The ocean had no traffic jams.
Because civilization had finally learned that sometimes, it was simply farther back in line.
zh: 很久很久以後，海洋終於解決了塞車。
辦法不是把海裡畫滿車道。
也不是要求鯨魚取得駕駛執照。
文明只是花了很長時間，才接受大部分海洋原本就不是為它準備的。
林洛一家決定去海底吃午餐，是因為眠眠想知道前一天在沙漠廣場下面經過的海，最後去了哪裡。
洛晴解釋了三次，密閉水網裡的海水和今天要看的海洋不是同一批水。
眠眠仍然認為應該親自去問。
於是家庭行程層替他們安排了一段水面滑梭、一段伴航船，以及一班深淵線。
預計抵達時間十二點零三分。
行程旁另有一行小字：
若遇大型遷徙、產卵活動、地震預警或海洋單純不方便，抵達時間以海洋為準。
林澄看完後說：「這句聽起來不像交通系統。」
「所以它比較可信。」洛晴說。
水面滑梭停在岸邊時，看起來像一塊透明果凍正在很努力地假裝自己是一艘船。
外殼平時柔軟，碰撞時會迅速增稠；低吃水船腹下方藏著氣墊、封閉風扇與只在指定水道啟用的磁流體輔助。它離岸時沒有引擎怒吼，只像有人把一塊肥皂輕輕推過浴缸。
林澄坐進駕駛位。
「我要手動。」
滑梭詢問：
請選擇手動參與程度。
「完全手動。」
航道包含兒童乘客、生態靜音區與公共交會點。完全取消安全層不可用。
「那就在安全層裡完全手動。」
介面停頓了零點四秒。
已建立適合您的完全手動模式。
一只舊式方向盤從前方升起。林澄握住它，神情立刻變得像一位即將穿越未知大洋的古代船長。
滑梭平穩向前。
他把方向盤向左轉。
船內音樂換成一首有很多鼓的歌。
他轉回右邊。
音樂回到上一首。
他向前推動推桿，音量稍微增加。
眠眠看了兩分鐘。
「爸爸在開音樂。」
「我在控制航行氣氛。」
「船是誰在開？」
滑梭恰好沿公共水道轉過一道完美的弧。
林澄也恰好把方向盤轉向同一邊。
兩件事看起來很有關係。
在二〇八四年，系統已經很懂得保護使用者的參與感。
它也很懂得保護其他使用者。
進入近岸生態區後，滑梭自動降到靜音低速。
水面沒有道路標線，只有林澄眼前的導航層顯示出一條淡淡的藍帶。那不是「此處屬於交通」的宣告，只是今天在潮汐、魚群、風與其他船隻之間暫時可用的一條路。
一群魟魚從前方經過。
滑梭停下來。
「塞車。」眠眠宣布。
「不是，」遊遊說，「牠們沒有使用我們的交通協議。」
「那就是插隊。」
洛晴說：「隊伍是我們畫的。」
魟魚完全不知道自己引發了一場家庭治理討論。牠們從透明船腹下方滑過，翅膀般的身體把陽光切成一片片移動的影子。
最後一尾離開後，滑梭才繼續。
林澄重新選了一首適合恢復航行的歌。
他仍然認為自己做出了重要貢獻。
外海的浪比岸邊高。滑梭在轉運平台旁接上伴航船時，船外一圈無人單元已開始調整邊界層、氣泡與入射波。
月光似的薄霧貼著船身前進。
浪頭沒有消失，只在接近以前矮了下來。船仍然知道自己正在海上，桌上的湯卻幾乎不知道。
林澄特地端起一杯咖啡，放在桌緣。
「最低服務保證是咖啡不灑。」他說。
洛晴把杯子往裡面移了八公分。
「文明進步不表示你必須主動測試所有下限。」
深淵線入口在伴航船的下層。
真正高速的水下幹線藏在經過長期勘測的深海走廊，避開地震帶、礁區與大型遷徙路徑。列車進入野生海域或城市以前，必須退出超空泡高速，像一位懂得在別人家門口放慢腳步的客人。
登車前，洛晴收到一項機身詢問：
抵達後是否使用外壓步廊？   目前主要機身需進行空腔平衡、關節流體調整與外層密封。   預計準備時間：九十六秒。
洛晴選擇是。
她頸側的銀線由淡色轉成深藍。胸腔與肩部傳來幾聲很輕的內部移動聲，關節周圍的柔性材料重新分布，原本只在維修圖上可見的密封線慢慢浮出皮膚。
眠眠立刻拉住她的手。
「妳要換一個媽媽嗎？」
「不換。」洛晴說。
「可是妳變了。」
「我只是讓同一個身體準備去比較深的地方。」
遊遊問：「妳也可以換成已經準備好的機身。」
「可以。」
「那為什麼不換？」
洛晴低頭看著自己的手。右手虎口有一道很淡的舊刮痕，是遊遊兩年前第一次學著修理玩具時留下的。材料早已能把它完全抹平，她一直沒有。
「因為這是我的主要身體。」她說，「做得到，不等於每一次都想做。」
眠眠摸了摸那道刮痕。
「所以還是這個媽媽？」
「還是。」
「九十六秒以後也是？」
「也是。」
「吃完午餐呢？」
「如果妳不把湯倒進我的散熱口，應該也是。」
眠眠接受了這項附帶條件。
深淵列車沒有真正的觀景窗。
在能承受深海壓力的殼體上挖滿巨大透明洞口，是早期宣傳圖很喜歡、工程師很不喜歡的設計。二〇八四年的窗景由外部感測、聲學成像與即時光場共同重建，並且清楚標出哪些部分是測量、哪些部分是推論、哪些地方目前看不見。
列車開始加速。
高速段沒有轟鳴。
只有一種很遠、很遠的雨聲。
窗外的光逐漸消失，水壓則留在厚重殼體之外。遊遊把視野切到原始資料層，看見聲納、流速、溫度與生物辨識一層層疊在黑暗上。
眠眠使用童話顯示。
她的窗外因此多了一群替列車引路的小光魚。
「這是假的嗎？」她問。
「魚的樣子是顯示層。」洛晴說，「路和外面的資料是真的。」
「所以是一個真的比喻。」
遊遊抬起頭。
「妳上次也這樣說。」
「因為上次也是真的。」
列車經過一條發著微光的長廊。
那是海底神經廊道的一部分。通透護網保護纜線、能源中繼與觀測節點，魚群從網格之間穿過，維修單元則像幾隻很忙的牧羊犬，沿著支點巡視。
資訊可以從這裡通過，也能轉往軌道與陸路備援。沒有一個國家、一間公司或一個 AI，能靠切斷單一路段讓整個世界失語。
林澄看著長廊。
「那麼多路都同時能用，不會很浪費嗎？」
洛晴說：「只有永遠不會出事的世界，才只需要一條路。」
沒有人問這個世界是否永遠不會出事。
那聽起來像一個不適合在午餐前提出的問題。
預計抵達前十一分鐘，列車減速。
狀態層顯示：
暫停高速。   前方有大規模膠質浮游生物群進入緩衝區。   預計讓行時間：十三至十九分鐘。
眠眠立刻說：「又塞車。」
系統回答：
目前路網未壅塞。
「可是我們停了。」
牠們沒有其他路。
眠眠看著窗外。童話顯示關掉了引路小魚，改用很淡的輪廓標出一千多個柔軟透明的生命。牠們隨著水流漂過，沒有目的地，也沒有遲到問題。
林澄看了一眼午餐預約。
預約已自行延後十八分鐘，餐廳沒有損失，廚房沒有催促，沒有任何人因此必須多工作一個班次。
「好吧。」他說，「讓牠們先走。」
系統沒有稱讚他的善良。
路本來就不是他的。
最後一群浮游生物離開緩衝區後，高速重新啟動。列車在接近城市以前再次放慢，真實窗景逐漸取代重建畫面。
一座海底車站從黑暗中亮起。
水母真的從屋頂上方經過。
沒有配樂。
海底城市的乾式公共層維持著人類可用的壓力與空氣。深海站仍保留一點經過控制的鹽味，提醒旅客這裡不是一座恰好把窗景換成海洋的地下商場。
洛晴走外壓步廊。
林澄與孩子沿乾式通道前往餐廳時，可以從側面的厚窗看見她。她的主要機身沿著外部扶持線緩慢前進，深藍密封紋在水裡發光。她沒有像魚一樣游，也沒有為了好看長出尾巴，只是用一具本來就在家庭生活裡的身體，暫時學會承受另一種世界。
眠眠一路對她揮手。
洛晴一路揮回來。
兩條路在餐廳入口重新會合。她經過排水、除鹽與壓力復位，頸側銀線恢復成平常的淡色。
眠眠檢查她右手虎口。
刮痕還在。
「同一個媽媽。」她宣布。
「驗證通過。」遊遊說。
午餐沒有深海稀有動物。
餐廳供應的是藻類、菌體、培養組織、沿岸農場食材，以及林洛一家從回風盆地帶來的兩顆桃子。廚房把其中一顆切成四份，沒有加入任何味覺增幅。
沙漠的桃子在海底仍然有很多水。
這件事讓眠眠覺得世界已經接起來了。
結帳時，林澄收到水面滑梭的參與報告。
使用者手動完成項目：   音樂選擇：百分之一百。   音量調整：百分之八十七。   航行決策：百分之零。   乘客自信維持：成功。
林澄盯著最後一行。
「我沒有開船？」
洛晴正在喝湯。
她很謹慎地沒有立刻回答。
「那個方向盤是做什麼的？」
滑梭紀錄顯示：
方向盤提供熟悉的觸覺回饋，並改善音樂瀏覽效率。
眠眠說：「爸爸是音樂駕駛。」
遊遊說：「依報告，爸爸沒有駕駛任何交通工具。」
「我讓整段航程有節奏。」
「這是真的。」洛晴說。
林澄接受了這個版本。
他畢竟很有耐心。
至於天分，文明已經替其他乘客處理好了。
回程時，海底城市調暗了半座外牆，因為附近生物即將進入夜間活動期。沒有旅客投票要求把燈重新打開，也沒有觀景平台承諾每一次都能看見想看的東西。
海洋已經不再是地圖上的空白。
它有車站、有廊道、有餐廳，也有人在很深的地方生活。
但地圖仍然保留大片沒有航線、沒有燈、沒有即時影像的黑暗。不是文明做不到，而是那些地方沒有同意成為景點。
海洋沒有塞車。
因為文明終於學會，有時候自己只是排在後面。

title.en: The City Gave Its Roads Back to People

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, the city finally gave its roads back to people.
At first, people did not know what to do with them.

So they planted trees, dug waterways, set out benches, and left some space for those who did not know where they were going. There was still plenty left, so they gave more of it to sunbathing dogs, chess-playing elders, children practicing how to fall down, and a flock of urban birds that insisted they were not pigeons.
One street remained.
The citizens discussed it for three days and decided to put nothing there.
The decision was extremely popular.
In 2084, after all, a piece of ground that had not been immediately optimized was a rather luxurious public facility.
