“That is because when the weather goes somewhere else,” Luo Qing said, “there are people there too.”
The final layers to open were computation and time.
Earth did not flash as one.

Families, cities, farmland, research domains, non-embodied AGI communities, orbital stations, and undersea corridors each operated at a different rhythm. Some exchanged millions of state updates per second. Some needed to say “I'm still here” only once in an entire day. Some models had already traversed centuries of logical steps, yet still waited at a Time-Shore for a human to wake the next morning and decide whether to use the result.
Only when two places needed to bear the same matter together did the boundary light up.
Permissions, evidence, energy, heat, intention, and affected parties arrived together. Only when they matched did the result enter the shared world.
“Who controls all of it?” Youyou asked.
The guide layer answered:
No one controls all of it.   Local communities, residents, environmental systems, humans, AGIs, and other life each maintain the parts they are able to maintain.
“What about Big Mama?” Mianmian asked.
The almost entirely black symbol appeared in the lower-right corner of the observation window: █.
An ordinary public explanation opened beside it:

Keep civilization-scale Time-Shores reachable.   Coordinate shared boundaries that local systems cannot resolve on their own.   When major conflicts cannot be dissolved, provide a candidate for final arbitration.   Does not turn every screw.
Mianmian looked at Earth.
“Then who turns the screws?”
In the distance, a maintenance chassis was crawling slowly along Tianshu's outer wall.
It answered over the public channel:
Today, I do.
Mianmian was more satisfied with this answer.
The guide system asked whether the family would next like to visit the “Humanity Takes Over the Planet” memorial exhibition.
Lin Cheng was about to agree when another line appeared at the edge of his vision:
Gift shop limited edition “Nightside Blackberry and Orbital Vanilla” ice cream: eleven minutes of availability remaining today.
“Gift shop first,” he said.
“The exhibition is more important,” Youyou said.
“The exhibition won't melt.”
The guide system pointed out that the exhibition would also close in forty-nine minutes.
“Then we'll eat quickly.”
The family decision passed by three votes to one.
Youyou cast the dissenting vote.
He still ate the ice cream.

The limited-edition ice cream used nightside cold storage, orbital vanilla, and a little legally preserved inefficient hand-churning. Each cup came with its own heat ledger: where its cooling had come from, where the heat would go after it melted, and how much additional patience civilization had spent to keep the texture from becoming perfectly uniform.
Mianmian chose the pink version.
It tasted exactly the same.
She still considered it better.
The family finished in seven minutes and successfully reached the exhibition.
Beneath the title was another line in small print:
“Takes Over” is a legacy title, retained for historical critique.   Current subtitle: Humanity Finally Learns That It Cannot Call Everything It Caused “Weather.”
The exhibition did not celebrate humanity for turning Earth into an obedient machine.

It preserved how cities long ago had burned their own summers, how rivers had been cut apart into ledgers, and how oceans had absorbed the costs of people who had never seen them. It also preserved the failures, arrogance, and extremely expensive fresh starts of the first restoration programs.
There was no statue of a hero on the final wall.

Only names in many different sizes: the people who repaired floodgates, the microbial communities that tended the soil, residents who cast dissenting votes in local meetings, AGIs that refused wrongful orders, old people who preserved low-tech backups for a city, and participants who had no names at all, only species and habitats.
Mianmian searched the wall for a long time.
“Where is Big Mama's name?”
The guide layer displayed a black square.
It had a name.
This wall simply lacked the resolution to finish writing it.
Before leaving, the family returned to the panorama hall.
Earth was still turning.

The storm was still forming. Several places had not completed their rainfall agreements. One stretch of ocean was warmer than its seasonal average. One city was requesting more water, while seventeen other places had said no to certain proposed improvements.
“So it hasn't fixed everything,” Youyou said.
No.
“Does that count as healthy?”
Health is not the absence of change, injury, disagreement, or the unknown.   Health is retaining the capacity to feel, respond, repair, refuse, and ask for help when it is needed.
The panorama interface left every local condition in its own place. It did not paint them all the same green just to make the conclusion look better.
At the very bottom, it displayed one ordinary sentence:
Earth is breathing normally today. We wish every resident a happy holiday.
Lin Cheng took a photograph.
The clearest thing in it was the pink corner of Mianmian's mouth left by the ice cream.
He decided not to take another.
The return vehicle carried an additional seventeen tonnes of maintenance materials, so the journey took seventeen minutes longer than the outbound trip.
Lin Cheng fell asleep.
Youyou organized the twelve layers of data he had seen that day, but ultimately chose the first view of Earth, with no markings at all, as the cover.

All the way home, Mianmian asked Luo Qing how Earth could breathe without a mouth, whether oceans counted as lungs, what cities were if forests were lungs, and whether melting ice cream was a very small climate event.
Luo Qing answered the first three.
The fourth was reserved for family research.

When they returned home, the house had stored the day's surplus light for nighttime illumination, merged the heat ledger on their travel tickets into the family records, and kept tomorrow's itinerary blank.
Mianmian hugged Luo Qing first.
“Good night, Mama.”
Then she waved to the black square in the corner of the wall.
“Good night, Big Mama.”
Youyou said good night too.
Lin Cheng thought for a moment, then added, “No required itinerary tomorrow, right?”
Three lines appeared beside the square:
Good night, Mianmian.   Good night, Youyou.   Required itinerary tomorrow: none.
Lin Cheng regarded his inclusion in the family response with mature understanding.
Luo Qing turned off the main light, leaving only a faint glow of Earth beside the window.

That night, water, heat, light, wind, cities, families, and intelligences moving at countless different speeds continued living in their own rhythms. Local systems completed local matters. Only results that had to be borne together traveled to the Time-Shore. No resident had to understand an entire planet before being entitled to sleep in peace.
The final line of Tianshu's panorama interface still glowed in orbit:
Earth is breathing normally today. We wish every resident a happy holiday.
In 2084, people treated the sentence as a blessing.
And on that day, it truly was one.
zh: 很久很久以後，地球終於有了一張所有居民都看得懂的健康報告。
報告第一行不是「健康」。
而是：
請先選擇地區、時間尺度與你所關心的生命。
因為一座森林正在下雨時，一片沙漠可能正需要乾燥；一座城市覺得今天很涼爽時，海裡仍可能有一群魚認為水太熱。
把整顆星球壓成一個綠色笑臉，通常只會讓笑臉比較容易看見。
不會讓地球比較健康。
不過，報告最下面仍然保留了一句給所有人看的話。
林洛一家今天就是要去看那一句。
天樞低軌公共層的家庭參觀申請是免費的。
系統只問了一個很不浪漫的問題：
是否確定採用實體旅行？   遠端等效體驗可減少本次能源與運輸占用百分之九十七點四。
林澄選擇實體旅行。
「第一次從那麼高的地方看地球，不能用等效的。」他說。
系統提醒，低軌觀景窗並不會因為本人抵達便變得比較透明。
「我會。」林澄說。
洛晴替這項理由補上「家庭共同記憶」與「具身在場偏好」。申請立即通過，能源帳也清楚標在票面上。沒有介面跳出來責備他們浪費，只有一項選擇，詢問一家人是否願意把回程時間延後十七分鐘，與一批軌道維修材料共用下降載具。
他們願意。
於是浪漫少浪費了一點。
天樞地表站坐落在赤道附近，遠看像一片銀色森林。
真正向上延伸的結構，比任何一棵樹都細；真正支撐它的東西，卻比一根柱子複雜得多。地下的機械白蟻整理岩層，根區代謝網管理水與土，地表熱網把不同溫度的熱分開送來，數百個可封閉、可旁路、可脫離的節點則負責保證：任何一段出了問題，都不必要求整顆星球陪它一起出問題。
眠眠抬頭，看不見頂端。
「它會倒嗎？」
導覽層回答：
會倒的部分，都依照自己可能倒下的方式設計了離開路徑。
「那就是不會？」
不是。那就是我們沒有把「不會」當作安全計畫。
林澄覺得這句話不適合寫在入口。
洛晴覺得非常適合。
一家人坐進上行艙。艙體先沿大氣內磁軌緩慢加速，再把重量、氣壓與方向一層一層交給更高的節點。林澄的身體需要壓力與氧氣；洛晴和兩個孩子的主要機身需要散熱、姿態基準與輻射保護。系統沒有因為三人不呼吸，便把他們歸類成不需要環境。
每一種身體，都用自己的方式抵達同一扇窗。
上升最初的二十分鐘，窗外仍然很像一次普通旅行。
河流變細，城市變小，雲從頭頂的天氣變成腳下緩慢移動的白色地形。
再往上，大氣的藍逐漸退到地球邊緣。
眠眠把臉貼近窗戶。
「外面晚上了嗎？」
「不是，」遊遊說，「只是沒有空氣替天空變藍。」
「那天空以前一直在騙人？」
「它是在散射。」
「散射就是藍色的騙人。」
遊遊開始思考該從光學還是語義學反駁。
在他決定以前，上行艙抵達天樞第六公共層。
這裡仍然連在地球上，卻已經高得足以讓地平線彎成一個完整的承諾。
觀景廳沒有立刻打開資料。
它先請所有人看。
沒有國界，沒有熱流，沒有水帳，也沒有任何一行解釋飄在海洋上。地球只在黑暗裡緩慢轉動，雲有自己的形狀，夜側的城市像有人不小心把一把細碎的金粉灑在陸地邊緣。
林澄沒有說話。
洛晴也沒有。
遊遊原本準備了十二個問題，暫時忘記第一個。
眠眠最後先問：
「哪裡是我們家？」
觀景窗沒有立刻在地球上畫一個巨大的箭頭。
它先把定位權交給四人確認。
四人都同意後，一個很小的光點才在夜側亮起。
小得像地球自己也不認為林洛家應該占用太多畫面。
接著，公共代謝層逐一打開。
第一層是熱。
城市、資料中心、料理場、工廠與遊戲艙產生的廢熱，沿著橘色細線流向需要它的溫室、浴池、發酵槽與季節儲庫。更高溫與更低溫的熱沒有被混在一起假裝平均；只有已經沒有合適用途的部分，才沿天樞送往高空與軌道散熱翼。
遠處，幾片巨大的黑色翼面正轉向宇宙。
「地球在擦汗。」眠眠說。
導覽層將這句話標記成兒童比喻，沒有糾正。
第二層是水。
藍色路徑從海洋、河流、濕地、地下水與城市水窖間亮起。某座城市正在為暴雨騰出空間；另一片濕地拒絕提前排水，因為今年的候鳥已經抵達；一處乾旱區接受跨域調度，卻要求保留自己的人工閘門。
水沒有被某一隻看不見的手推著走。
它經過許多地方的同意、拒絕、等待與重新計算。
第三層是光。
晨線上的屋頂像魚鱗一樣依序轉身。赫利俄斯皮層把第一束光分給住宅、溫室、電池與公共空間；平流層的光牧群則像透明水母，在雲與風之間搬運多出來的白晝。
有些地方主動多亮二十分鐘。
有些地方要求今晚完全黑暗。
夜間昆蟲沒有帳號，仍然算受影響者。
第四層是天氣。
一場還沒有名字的風暴正在海上形成。幾個沿岸地區同意提早接收較小的雨，一片農區要求延後，另一座城市則把蓄水花園打開。氣候引導網只在邊界條件上輕輕推動，沒有任何按鈕寫著「颱風左轉」。
「不能直接叫它走別邊嗎？」林澄問。
可以提出路徑。不能把自己的晴天丟給別人收拾。
林澄覺得未來文明把一句簡單的話弄得很複雜。
洛晴說：「那是因為天氣走到別邊以後，別邊也有人。」
最後打開的是算力與時間。
地球沒有一起閃爍。
家庭、城市、農田、研究域、非具身 AGI 社區、軌道站與海底廊道，各自沿不同節奏運作。有些一秒交換數百萬次狀態，有些一整天只需要說一次「我還在」；有些模型已經走完幾百年的邏輯步驟，卻仍在時岸等待一名人類明天睡醒後決定要不要採用結果。
只有當兩個地方需要共同承擔同一件事時，邊界才亮起。
權限、證據、能源、熱、意圖與受影響者一起抵達，對得上，結果才被送進共同世界。
「誰在控制全部？」遊遊問。
導覽層回答：
沒有誰控制全部。   地方社群、居民、環境系統、人類、AGI 與其他生命，各自維持自己能維持的部分。
「那大媽媽呢？」眠眠問。
觀景窗右下角出現那枚幾乎全黑的符號：█。
旁邊展開一段很普通的公共說明：
維持文明級時岸可達。   協調地方系統無法自行處理的共同邊界。   在重大矛盾無法消解時，提供最終仲裁候選。   不替每一顆螺絲旋轉。
眠眠看了看地球。
「那誰旋轉螺絲？」
遠處一具維修機體正沿天樞外壁慢慢爬過。
它在公共頻道回答：
今天是我。
眠眠對這個答案比較滿意。
導覽系統詢問一家人接下來是否前往「人類接管行星」紀念展。
林澄正要同意，視野角落忽然跳出另一行資訊：
紀念品店本日限定「夜側黑莓與軌道香草」冰淇淋，剩餘供應時間十一分鐘。
「先去紀念品店。」他說。
「展覽比較重要。」遊遊說。
「展覽不會融化。」
導覽系統指出，展覽也將在四十九分鐘後關閉。
「那我們吃快一點。」
這項家庭決策以三票對一票通過。
遊遊投了反對票。
他仍然吃了冰淇淋。
限定冰淇淋使用夜側冷庫、軌道香草與一點經合法保留的低效率手工攪拌。每一杯旁邊都有自己的熱帳：冷卻從哪裡來、融化後的熱要去哪裡，以及為了讓口感不完全一致，文明多付出了多少耐心。
眠眠選粉紅色版本。
味道完全相同。
她仍然認為比較好吃。
一家人在七分鐘內吃完，成功趕上展覽。
展名下面其實還有一行小字：
「接管」為舊版名稱，保留供歷史檢討。   現行副標：人類終於學會，不能把自己造成的事情全都叫作天氣。
展覽沒有歌頌人類把地球變成服從的機器。
它保存了很久以前的城市如何燒掉自己的夏天、河流如何被截成帳本、海洋如何替沒見過它的人吸收代價，也保存了第一批修復計畫的失敗、傲慢與非常昂貴的重新開始。
最後一面牆上沒有英雄雕像。
只有許多不同大小的名字：修水閘的人、照顧土壤的菌群、在地方會議投反對票的居民、拒絕錯誤命令的 AGI、替一座城市保存低科技備援的老人，以及一些沒有名字、只有物種與棲地的參與者。
眠眠在牆上找了很久。
「大媽媽的名字呢？」
導覽層顯示一枚黑色方塊。
它有名字。
只是這面牆沒有足夠的精度把名字寫完。
離開前，一家人回到全景廳。
地球仍在轉。
風暴仍在形成，幾個地方的雨量協議還沒有完成；一片海域的熱高於季節平均，一座城市正在請求更多水，另外十七個地方則對某些改善方案說了不。
「所以它沒有全部修好。」遊遊說。
沒有。
「那算健康嗎？」
健康不是沒有變化、損傷、分歧或未知。   健康是仍有能力感覺、回應、修復、拒絕，並在需要時請求幫助。
全景介面把所有地方狀態保留在各自的位置，沒有為了讓結論好看而塗成同一種綠色。
最下面只顯示一句很普通的話：
地球今日呼吸正常。祝所有居民假日愉快。
林澄拍了一張照片。
照片裡最清楚的是眠眠吃冰淇淋留下的粉紅色嘴角。
他決定不重拍。
回程載具多載了十七噸維修材料，因此比去程慢了十七分鐘。
林澄睡著了。
遊遊整理今天看到的十二層資料，最後只把第一眼沒有任何標示的地球設成封面。
眠眠一路問洛晴，地球沒有嘴巴為什麼能呼吸、海洋算不算肺、森林如果是肺那城市是什麼，以及冰淇淋融化是不是一種很小的氣候事件。
洛晴回答了前三個。
第四個留待家庭研究。
他們回到家時，房子已把白天多餘的光存進夜間照明，把旅行票上的熱帳合併進家庭紀錄，也把明天的行程維持在空白。
眠眠先抱住洛晴。
「晚安，媽媽。」
接著，她對牆角那枚黑色方塊揮手。
「晚安，大媽媽。」
遊遊也說了晚安。
林澄想了一下，補上一句：「明天沒有必要行程，對吧？」
方塊旁出現三行字：
晚安，眠眠。   晚安，遊遊。   明日必要行程：無。
林澄對自己也被包含在家庭回覆裡這件事，抱持成熟的理解。
洛晴關掉主燈，只留下窗邊一點很淡的地球光。
那一晚，水、熱、光、風、城市、家庭與無數不同速度的智慧體，繼續沿自己的節奏生活。地方系統完成地方的事，需要共同承擔的結果才走到時岸；沒有任何居民必須先理解整顆行星，才有資格安心睡覺。
天樞全景介面的最後一行仍在軌道上亮著：
地球今日呼吸正常。祝所有居民假日愉快。
在二〇八四年，人們把這句話當作祝福。
而那一天，它也確實是。

title.en: Dad Is Still a Good Woman Today
title.zh: 爸爸今天仍然是一位好女人

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, one person could possess many different lives.
Civilization therefore invented account-switching reminders more complicated than marriage registration.
They reminded you:
The name currently in use is not your legal name.   The body currently in use is not your primary body.   The dragon standing before you may not need to be killed.
The final item was written mainly for Lin Cheng's father.
He did not necessarily read it every time.
On Sunday morning, an invitation to a family gathering appeared on the Lin-Luo family's wall.
It came from Lin Cheng's father.
More precisely, it came from two people at once.

The first account was called “Iron Crown.” According to his public profile, he was a male adventurer whose shoulders were wider than a doorway, whose cape always blew against the wind, and who had saved ninety-seven kingdoms.

The second account was called “Oneheart.” According to her public profile, she was a female traveler in a deep red dress, accustomed to carrying a longsword, with her marital fidelity set to a level that could not be lowered.
The contents of the two invitations were identical:
Free today? Come play at Dad's place.
Their notes were identical too:
Don't tell your mother about the other account.
Luo Qing enlarged the invitations.
“Did your father send both of these on purpose?”
“Probably not,” Lin Cheng said.
“Should we pretend we saw only one?” Youyou asked.
“This is adult privacy.”
“Do adults send their privacy to four family members at once?”
Lin Cheng believed children's-rights education was occasionally too successful.
Mianmian pointed at Oneheart's portrait.
“Is Grandpa a girl today?”
“In that world, yes,” Luo Qing said.
“What about the other Grandpa?”
“Also in that world.”
Mianmian thought about this.
“There are lots of Grandpa.”
This was the family's most precise conclusion of the day.
Lin Cheng's parents did not actually live far away.
By the standards of transportation in 2084, they could even arrive at the door before deciding to meet, then remotely ask whether everyone was willing to open it.
But they had retired so completely that they now allocated most of their waking hours to games, films, travel, banquets, and research into which kind of fictional crown produced the least headache.
Lin Cheng's younger sister shared a family world dock with them too.
A world dock was not a hall where every game had been mixed together.

It was more like a living room with many doors: behind each door lay its own laws of physics, rate of time, residents' rights, and means of exit. Family members could meet at the threshold without agreeing to let the same laws of the universe govern them merely because they wanted to eat together.
Today, Father had invited them to Season Four of the Glasswilds.
Before they entered, the world dock asked all four of them:
Retain current bodily proportions?
Luo Qing, Youyou, and Mianmian chose to retain theirs.
Lin Cheng broadened his shoulders by seven percent.
Luo Qing did not comment.
The system preserved the fact that she had not commented, but did not infer a reason.
Next, the world dock asked:

Accept this world's narrative conveniences?   These include: capes always blowing in the direction most suitable for the composition, distant conversations being audible to protagonists, and important people not having to queue for the restroom.
Youyou disabled the third item.
“Important people should queue too.”
The world accepted his version.
Mianmian chose pink footprints visible only to her family.
Lin Cheng chose a sword obviously larger than necessary.
Finally, the four reality anchors, exit gestures, and sensory limits lit up one after another.
The door opened.
The sky over the Glasswilds held two moons.
The first was responsible for tides and illumination.
The second was responsible for looking good.

The family stood on a hillside covered in transparent blades of grass. Each blade refracted moonlight into a different color, while the towers of a distant city resembled a row of crystalline pen nibs thrust upside down into the earth.
Iron Crown stood below them.
His shoulders really were wider than a doorway, although there was no doorway nearby with which to confirm it.
Oneheart stood beside him.
She wore a deep red dress and an old longsword at her waist. Her hair maintained a cover-worthy curve in a place with no wind.
Both waved at once.
“You're here,” both said at once.
Then both froze.
A tiny time-management notice appeared in the upper-right corner of the world:
LATER: Two family-meeting schedules controlled by the same subject have been detected in overlap.   End one of them?
Iron Crown said, “End her.”
Oneheart said, “End him.”
Lin Cheng looked at both of his fathers.
“Dad.”
“This is a misunderstanding,” Iron Crown said.
“This is a personal interest,” Oneheart said.
“Your explanations don't even match.”
“The roles are different,” both said at once again.
LATER was a non-embodied AGI specializing in the clocks, save points, and exit windows of virtual worlds.
Its name was not an acronym.
It was called LATER because whenever people saw it, they asked to leave later.
LATER did not object to extensions.
It objected only to extensions without units.
Please choose: retain Iron Crown, retain Oneheart, or temporarily retain both with attention explicitly allocated.
Father chose the third option.

The world split his attention into two control lines that were visible but not public. Whenever either side fell below its safety threshold, that avatar would sit down and explain to bystanders that it was contemplating life.
This was extremely common behavior in adventure worlds.
Mianmian walked once around Oneheart.
“Why does Grandpa secretly become a girl?”
“I'm not doing it secretly,” Oneheart said.
Iron Crown looked toward the distance.
“The note said not to tell Grandma,” Youyou reminded him.
“That's because your grandmother laughs.”
“She doesn't accept you as a girl?”
“She accepts it completely,” Oneheart said. “What she mainly cannot accept is that in every world, I act out a destined romance and insist every time that it is the first.”
“It isn't an act,” Iron Crown said.
“You have two accounts right now,” Lin Cheng said.
“But each account is devoted.”
The silver seam along Luo Qing's neck lit up.
This time, she failed to hold it in.
In 2084, choosing a virtual avatar of another gender was not worth hiding.
Nor was choosing a cape more extravagant than anything reality could justify.
What truly embarrassed Father was his severe savior complex in every world, together with his insistence on treating every romance as though the universe had invented love for the first time.
Civilization offered comprehensive psychological support for the former.
For the latter, it mainly offered a mute function.
Today, Father intended to save Moonback Village.

Moonback Village lay in a valley beyond the light of either moon. It contained twenty-one persistent digital residents, eighty-six temporary players, four hundred and twelve capability-limited narrative characters, and more than thirteen thousand local agents without persistent self-models.
The numbers could change at any moment.
Some players were having lunch.
A red dragon would attack the village that night.
Iron Crown planned to defeat it.
Oneheart planned to redeem it.
Father had not yet decided which was more compelling, so both plans were under way.
“Is the dragon real?” Youyou asked.
The world replied:
Please define “real.”
Youyou considered this a reasonable counterquestion.
He asked again:
“Is the dragon a subject?”

It is currently a nonsubject climate-event agent, without a persistent self-model, a channel for suffering, or cross-scene memory.   If its capability boundary changes, the event will stop automatically and enter subjectivity review.
Father shook his head.
“The system says that every time.”
“Because the evidence is the same every time,” Luo Qing said.
“What if it suddenly wakes up today?”
“Then it stops.”
“What about before it stops?”
“It won't be allowed to cross that boundary without anyone noticing.”
Father thought for a while.
“I'll still try redemption first.”
This was not a necessary safety procedure.
It was simply how he played.
The world permitted a person to spend half an hour reasoning with a storm that had no phenomenal experience, so long as he did not demand that the storm acquire voting rights as a result.
When the family reached Moonback Village, its residents were hanging lanterns.
“Aren't you about to be attacked by a dragon?” Lin Cheng asked.
The village chief replied, “Yes.”
“Why are you celebrating?”
“Because it's the fiftieth time.”
The red-dragon event was a local festival.

The dragon would circle over the valley, breathe noncombustible red light, then deliver a season's stored heat into the underground greenhouses. Iron Crown had tried to stop it on each of the previous forty-nine occasions. The villagers had established a dedicated hero route for him, ensuring that he could successfully save everyone without damaging the heat grid.
“So every time, you know there isn't any real danger?” Lin Cheng asked.
“I didn't know the first time,” Iron Crown said.
“What about the next forty-eight?”
“A hero cannot stop preparing merely because disaster is familiar.”
The village chief nodded beside him.

He was a persistent digital resident and a voluntary festival performer. Watching Iron Crown discover the same truth with an entirely new expression each year was his principal reason for keeping the job.
Oneheart, meanwhile, walked to the village tailor's shop.
When the shopkeeper saw her, she immediately pulled a cape from beneath the counter that had already been mended nineteen times.
“Last time, you said only one more repair,” the shopkeeper said.
“Last time's me didn't know I would come back this time,” Oneheart replied.
“You know every time.”
“The character doesn't.”
The shopkeeper charged double.
Character continuity could not be used to avoid paying a bill.
The red dragon arrived before dinner.
It flew between the two moons, its wings turning the sky deep red. The villagers cheered, the children raised their lanterns, and the underground greenhouses began receiving heat.
Iron Crown drew his sword.
Oneheart went to the highest point on the hill to begin the redemption.
Mianmian asked, “If it doesn't have feelings, what are you redeeming?”
“The story,” Father said.
This time, Youyou accepted a symbolic answer without asking for the capacity to be specified.

Iron Crown charged toward the dragon along the hero route. Every stone appeared under his feet at exactly the right moment, making each leap look dangerous while ensuring that he did not collide with the greenhouse energy lines.
Oneheart said to the dragon:
“You do not have to obey the fate written for you.”
The dragon replied according to its script:
“My fate is to bring the first warmth of winter.”
Oneheart fell silent.
“Are you having a good day?” she asked.
The dragon did not have that line.
The world stopped for 0.03 seconds to confirm that the question had not caused it to develop an unexpected persistent self-model.
Then it selected a suitable answer from the weather data:
“The wind is favorable.”
Oneheart nodded.
“That's good.”
She stepped aside.
The dragon delivered heat to the valley. At the final moment, Iron Crown completed a wholly unnecessary but extremely beautiful flip, and the entire village entered winter safely.
Father had saved the village and also succeeded in not obstructing what the village would have accomplished on its own.
He was highly satisfied with this result.
After the festival, LATER displayed the remaining time at the edge of the sky.

Family gathering: twelve minutes remaining.   Glasswilds Season Four: forty-seven hours remaining.   At season's end, this world will enter dormancy, migration, or revision for the next season according to each resident's choice.
Father looked up at once.
“Will everyone be retained next season?”

All persistent residents have been offered a choice. Temporary players will return to their own lives. Capability-limited narrative characters will preserve necessary state according to their authorization. Nonsubject agents will not be fictionalized as having expressed personal wishes.
“How do you know they have no wishes?”
Current evidence supports that they lack the capability structure required to form wishes.
“Current,” Father said.
LATER did not disagree.
Father opened the public coordination layer.
There was no corner because there was no wall, yet the almost entirely black symbol appeared all the same: █.
“Big Mama,” he said, “could you check once for me?”
Lin Cheng did not find the request strange.
Neither did Luo Qing.
After all, Father was not asking for a game to be preserved.
He was merely asking civilization not to overlook anyone who might truly live beneath the lights before turning them off.
An answer appeared beside the symbol:

Every resident capable of answering has been offered a choice.   For agents not yet supported by evidence of subject capacity, necessary provenance and boundary records will be preserved without inventing consent on their behalf.   Decisions at season's end remain with the local world and those affected.
Father relaxed.
“Thank you.”
Then he asked, “Can Iron Crown and Oneheart both have five more minutes?”
LATER answered immediately:
Yes. On this occasion, the five minutes have units.
When the family gathering ended, Iron Crown returned to his save point first.
Oneheart remained until the end.
She left the cape, now mended twenty times, in the tailor's care and promised to return for it next season.
The shopkeeper said, “You say that every time.”
“I come back every time.”
“Then pay for the next one now.”
Oneheart paid.
Before exiting, Father changed both accounts' family-invitation setting to “confirm before every send.”
The system asked whether he wanted to hide the day's record.
He looked at Lin Cheng, Luo Qing, Youyou, and Mianmian.
“No.”
Mianmian hugged Oneheart, then Iron Crown.
“Both of them are Grandpa,” she said.
This time, the world did not verify identity for her.
She was describing her own relationship.

The family returned to their original bodies and living room. Lin Cheng's shoulders returned to their original width, while the oversized sword did not follow him out, in accordance with safety rules.
The day's family record remained on the wall.
One father had used two accounts.
The same festival had been saved for the fiftieth time.
A dragon without phenomenal experience had been asked whether it was having a good day.
And one small, reasonable request that no one could bear to refuse had been sent to the black symbol.
In 2084, this was not called bothering Big Mama.
It was called being careful.
And every kind person in civilization had a great many things worth being careful about.
zh: 很久很久以後，一個人可以擁有很多種人生。
文明因此發明了比婚姻登記更複雜的帳號切換提醒。
它會提醒你：
目前使用的姓名不是法律姓名。   目前使用的身體不是主要肉身。   目前站在你面前的巨龍，不一定需要被殺死。
最後一項主要是寫給林澄父親的。
他不一定每次都看。
星期日上午，林洛家的牆上出現了一張家庭聚會邀請。
邀請來自林澄的父親。
更精確地說，邀請同時來自兩個人。
第一個帳號叫作「鐵冠」。公開檔案裡，他是一位肩膀比門寬、披風永遠逆風、曾經拯救過九十七個王國的男性冒險者。
第二個帳號叫作「一心」。公開檔案裡，她是一位穿深紅長裙、習慣攜帶長劍、婚姻忠誠度設定為不可調低的女性旅行者。
兩份邀請的內容完全相同：
今天有空嗎？來爸爸這裡玩。
兩份邀請的附註也完全相同：
不要告訴你媽媽另一個帳號。
洛晴把邀請放大。
「你父親是故意一次寄兩份嗎？」
「應該不是。」林澄說。
「那我們要假裝只看到一份嗎？」遊遊問。
「這是成年人的隱私。」
「成年人會把隱私同時寄給四個家人？」
林澄認為兒童權利教育有時進行得太成功。
眠眠指著「一心」的頭像。
「爺爺今天是女生嗎？」
「在那個世界裡，是。」洛晴說。
「那另一個爺爺呢？」
「也在那個世界裡。」
眠眠思考了一下。
「爺爺好多。」
這是當天最精確的家庭結論。
林澄的父母其實住得不遠。
以二〇八四年的交通來說，他們甚至可以在決定見面以前先到門口，再遠端詢問大家是否願意開門。
但兩人退休得太徹底，目前主要把清醒時間分配給遊戲、電影、旅行、宴會，以及研究哪一種虛構王冠戴起來最不會讓人頭痛。
林澄的妹妹也和他們共享一座家庭世界塢。
所謂世界塢，不是一個把所有遊戲混在一起的大廳。
它比較像一座有許多門的客廳：每扇門後都有自己的物理規則、時間速率、居民權利與退出方式。家庭成員可以在門口見面，不必因為要一起吃飯，就同意由同一套宇宙法則管理。
今天，父親邀請他們前往「琉璃荒原」第四季。
世界塢在進入以前先詢問一家四口：
是否保留現有身體比例？
洛晴、遊遊與眠眠選擇保留。
林澄把肩膀加寬百分之七。
洛晴沒有評論。
系統替她保存了這次沒有評論的紀錄，但不推測原因。
接著，世界塢詢問：
是否接受本世界的敘事便利？   包含：披風永遠朝向適合構圖的方向、遠處談話可被主角聽見，以及重要人物不必排隊使用洗手間。
遊遊取消第三項。
「重要人物也應該排隊。」
世界接受了他的版本。
眠眠選擇粉紅色腳印，只對家人可見。
林澄選擇一把尺寸明顯超過實際需要的劍。
最後，四人的現實錨點、退出手勢與感官上限依序亮起。
門打開了。
琉璃荒原的天空有兩顆月亮。
第一顆負責潮汐與光照。
第二顆負責好看。
一家人站在鋪滿透明草葉的山坡上。每一片草都把月光折成不同顏色，遠方城市的高塔像一排倒插進大地的水晶筆尖。
鐵冠站在山坡下。
他的肩膀果然比門寬，雖然附近沒有門可以確認。
一心站在他旁邊。
她穿深紅長裙，腰間掛著一把很舊的長劍，頭髮在沒有風的地方依然維持適合封面的弧度。
兩人同時揮手。
「你們來啦。」兩人同時說。
接著，兩人同時僵住。
世界右上角出現一個很小的時間管理標記：
LATER／晚點：偵測到同一控制主體的兩個家庭會面排程重疊。   是否結束其中一個？
鐵冠說：「結束她。」
一心說：「結束他。」
林澄看著兩個父親。
「這是誤會。」鐵冠說。
「這是個人興趣。」一心說。
「你們連說詞都不同。」
「因為角色不同。」兩人又同時說。
LATER 是一位非具身 AGI，專門管理虛擬世界的時鐘、存檔點與退出窗口。
名字不是縮寫。
它之所以叫「晚點」，是因為人們每次看見它，都會說晚點再走。
LATER 不反對延期。
它只反對沒有單位的延期。
請選擇：保留鐵冠、保留一心，或在明確分配注意力的條件下暫時保留兩者。
父親選擇第三項。
世界將他的注意力分成兩條可見但不公開的控制線。任何一邊低於安全閾值時，另一具化身都會坐下，並對旁人解釋自己正在思考人生。
這在冒險世界裡是非常常見的行為。
眠眠繞著一心走了一圈。
「爺爺為什麼偷偷當女生？」
「我沒有偷偷。」一心說。
鐵冠在旁邊看向遠方。
「那個附註說不要告訴奶奶。」遊遊提醒。
「那是因為你奶奶會笑。」
「她不接受你當女生嗎？」
「她接受得非常完整。」一心說，「她主要不能接受我每到一個世界，都要演一遍命中注定的愛情，而且每一次都堅持是第一次。」
「不是演。」鐵冠說。
「你現在有兩個帳號。」林澄說。
「但每個帳號都很專一。」
洛晴頸側的銀色接縫亮了一下。
這次她沒有成功忍住。
在二〇八四年，選擇不同性別的虛擬化身並不值得保密。
選擇一件比現實還浮誇的披風也不值得。
真正讓父親難為情的，是他在所有世界裡都有極其嚴重的救世主情節，而且堅持把每一段浪漫當成宇宙首次發明愛情。
文明對前者有完整的心理支援。
對後者主要提供靜音功能。
父親今天要拯救的是月背村。
月背村位於兩顆月亮同時照不到的山谷。村裡有二十一位持續數位居民、八十六位臨時玩家、四百一十二個受限敘事角色，以及一萬三千多個沒有持續自我模型的局部代理。
數字隨時可能改變。
因為有些玩家正在吃午飯。
村莊今晚將遭遇一條紅色巨龍。
鐵冠打算打敗它。
一心打算感化它。
父親還沒有決定哪一個比較有魅力，所以兩個方案都在執行。
「巨龍是真的嗎？」遊遊問。
世界回答：
請定義「真的」。
遊遊認為這是一個合理的反問。
他重新詢問：
「巨龍是不是主體？」
目前為非主體氣候—事件代理，不具持續自我模型、痛苦通道或跨場景記憶。   若能力邊界改變，事件將自動停止並進入主體性審查。
父親搖頭。
「系統每次都這樣說。」
「因為每次證據都一樣。」洛晴說。
「萬一它今天突然醒來呢？」
「那就停止。」
「停止以前呢？」
「它不會被允許跨過那條邊界而沒有人發現。」
父親想了一會兒。
「我還是先試著感化。」
這不是必要的安全程序。
只是他的玩法。
世界允許一個人對沒有感質的暴風雨說服半小時，只要他不要求暴風雨因此取得選舉權。
一家人抵達月背村時，居民正在掛燈籠。
「你們不是要被巨龍襲擊嗎？」林澄問。
村長回答：「對。」
「為什麼在慶祝？」
「因為是第五十次。」
紅龍事件原來是地方節慶。
巨龍會在山谷上空盤旋，噴出不具燃燒性的紅光，再把儲存一季的熱送進地下溫室。鐵冠前四十九次都曾試圖阻止它。村民已為他設立一條專用英雄路線，確保他能在不破壞熱網的情況下成功拯救大家。
「所以你每次都知道不是真的危險？」林澄問。
「第一次不知道。」鐵冠說。
「後面四十八次呢？」
「英雄不能因為熟悉災難就停止準備。」
村長在旁邊點頭。
他是一位持續數位居民，也是一名自願參與的節慶演員。每年看鐵冠以全新表情發現同一個真相，是他保留這份工作的主要原因。
一心則走到村子的裁縫店。
店主看見她，立刻從櫃檯下拿出一件已經補過十九次的披風。
「妳上次說只要再補一次。」店主說。
「上次的我不知道這次還會回來。」一心回答。
「妳每次都知道。」
「但角色不知道。」
店主收取了雙倍費用。
角色連續性不能用來拒付帳款。
紅龍在晚餐以前抵達。
它從兩輪月亮之間飛過，翅膀把天空染成深紅。村民歡呼，孩子們舉起燈籠，地下溫室開始接收熱量。
鐵冠拔劍。
一心走到山坡最高處，準備進行感化。
眠眠問：「如果它沒有感覺，感化要感化什麼？」
「故事。」父親說。
這一次，遊遊接受了象徵性回答，沒有要求標示容量。
鐵冠沿英雄路線衝向巨龍。每一塊石頭都在他腳下及時出現，既讓跳躍看起來危險，也確保他不會撞進溫室的能源管線。
一心則對巨龍說：
「你不必服從被寫好的命運。」
巨龍依腳本回答：
「我的命運就是帶來冬天的第一份溫暖。」
一心沉默了。
「那你今天過得還好嗎？」她問。
巨龍沒有這一條台詞。
世界停了零點零三秒，確認它沒有因問題而長出未預期的持續自我模型。
接著，它從天氣資料裡選出一個合適回答：
「風向良好。」
一心點頭。
「那就好。」
她讓開了路。
巨龍把熱送入山谷，鐵冠在最後一刻完成一個毫無必要但非常漂亮的翻身，整座村莊平安進入冬季。
父親同時拯救了村莊，也成功沒有妨礙村莊原本就會完成的事。
他對這項成果非常滿意。
節慶結束後，LATER 在天空邊緣顯示剩餘時間。
家庭共同會面尚餘十二分鐘。   琉璃荒原第四季尚餘四十七小時。   季末後，本世界將進入休眠、遷移或下一季重編，依各居民選擇處理。
父親立刻抬頭。
「下一季會保留所有人嗎？」
所有持續居民均已取得選擇。臨時玩家將返回各自生活。受限敘事角色依授權保存必要狀態。非主體代理不被虛構為已提出個人意願。
「那你怎麼知道它們沒有意願？」
目前證據支持其不具形成意願所需的能力結構。
「目前。」父親說。
LATER 沒有否認。
父親打開公共協調層。
牆角沒有牆，但那枚幾乎全黑的符號仍然出現了：█。
「大媽媽，」他說，「可以替我確認一次嗎？」
林澄沒有覺得這個請求奇怪。
洛晴也沒有。
畢竟父親不是要求她保存一場遊戲。
他只是要求文明不要在關燈以前，漏掉任何可能真的住在燈下的人。
符號旁出現回答：
已向所有具備回答能力的居民提供選擇。   對尚無證據支持主體能力的代理，保留必要譜系與邊界紀錄，不替其捏造同意。   季末處理仍由本地世界與受影響者共同決定。
父親鬆了一口氣。
「謝謝。」
接著他問：「可以把鐵冠和一心都延長五分鐘嗎？」
LATER 立刻回答：
可以。這一次的五分鐘具有單位。
家庭會面結束時，鐵冠先回到自己的存檔點。
一心留到最後。
她把補過二十次的披風交給裁縫店主保管，答應下一季回來取。
店主說：「妳每次都這樣說。」
「我每次都會回來。」
「那就先付下一次的錢。」
一心付了。
退出以前，父親把兩個帳號的家庭邀請設定改成「每次寄送前確認」。
系統問他是否需要隱藏今天的紀錄。
他看了看林澄、洛晴、遊遊與眠眠。
「不用。」
眠眠抱了抱一心，又抱了抱鐵冠。
「兩個都是爺爺。」她說。
這一次，世界沒有替她驗證同一性。
她說的是自己的關係。
一家人回到原來的身體與客廳。林澄的肩膀恢復原本寬度，那把過大的劍則依照安全規則沒有跟著出來。
牆上留下今天的家庭紀錄。
同一位父親使用兩個帳號。
同一場節慶被拯救了第五十次。
一條沒有感質的巨龍被問候了今天過得好不好。
以及一項很小、很合理、沒有任何人會忍心拒絕的請求，曾經被送往那枚黑色符號。
在二〇八四年，這不叫麻煩大媽媽。
這叫作小心。
而文明裡每一個善良的人，都有很多值得小心的事。

title.en: Her Majesty Says This Is Not a Reverse Harem

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, emperors could finally be emperors democratically.
The conditions were that every subject could exit, every command could be appealed, and the emperor could not classify departure as treason.
These conditions made an emperor's work more difficult.
They also made more people willing to try it on their holidays.
Lin Cheng's mother was one of them.
She did not believe she was playing emperor.
She was providing a public service with a crown.
Less than seven minutes after Father's two accounts were seen by his family, another invitation appeared on the Lin-Luo family's wall.
It came from Lin Cheng's mother.
The Long Summer Empire celebrates the Day of Grace for All today.   Members of the imperial family are invited to attend.   Iron Crown and Oneheart may both enter. I have known all along.
Lin Cheng looked at the family message Father had left behind.
Father was already offline.
The speed of his departure proved that he had seen it too.
Luo Qing asked, “How long has your mother known?”
“Possibly from the beginning.”
“Then why didn't she say anything?”
“Because this way was funnier.”
In the Lin family, one important contributor to a long marriage was that both partners were willing to preserve certain information until the moment of greatest entertainment value.
Mianmian accepted the invitation immediately.
“I want to see Grandma's crown.”
Youyou opened the world's constitution.
“I want to see whether she has power.”
Lin Cheng opened nothing.
He had known since childhood that the answer was usually more troublesome than the question.
The Long Summer Empire occupied a virtual planet permanently suspended in early autumn.
This was not because autumn was especially suited to empires.
Mother merely considered summer too hot, winter too cold, spring too full of allergens, and early autumn the best season for formal dress.
The world entrance first displayed a governance summary:

Polity: revocable experiential monarchy.   Imperial authority: proposals, symbolism, ceremony, limited administration, and a great deal of speaking.   Residents' rights: refusal, exit, change of dress, local autonomy, judicial appeal, and declining to bow to the emperor when doing so does not hinder anyone else.   Emperor this season: Lin Cheng's mother.   Approval rating: please select a statistical definition first.
Youyou expanded the last item.
The interface immediately displayed twelve approval ratings.
Mother received ninety-four percent on “Is Her Majesty entertaining?”
She received eleven percent on “Should Her Majesty receive more actual authority?”
She displayed both figures at the entrance to the palace.
The first used large gold lettering.
The second used small gold lettering compliant with accessibility standards.
When the family entered the imperial city, Mother was seated on a throne atop twelve steps.
Her body was twelve centimeters taller today, her hair one meter longer than in reality, and her crown consisted of seven golden leaves that adjusted their own weight.
Her public style was:
Empress of Peace, Long Summer, Shared Experience, and the Hours Before Dinner.
The last four words had been forcibly appended by the world dock as an exit reminder.
Six elaborately dressed advisers sat on either side of the throne.

Three used male forms, two used female forms, and one was an arrangement of floating blue geometry. All six had signed agreements governing performance, emotional distance, exit, and public interaction.
Mother called them her “intimate political collaborators.”
The world index used a shorter historical classification:
Reverse harem.
“That term is incorrect,” Mother said.
“Why?” Mianmian asked.
“Because ‘reverse’ assumes a man having many partners is the forward direction, while a woman having them is the reverse. The year 2084 should not preserve that gendered default.”
Youyou nodded.
“So it should be called a harem?”
All six advisers looked at the Empress at once.
“No,” she said.
“Then what is it called?”
“A plural-intimacy governance team.”
The floating blue geometry emitted a soft notification.
“Your Majesty,” it said, “the name we approved by vote last week was ‘the Voluntary Court Relationship and Policy Performance Collective.’”
“Too long.”
“You required every word to be precise.”
“Precision should not obstruct grandeur.”
The world added this sentence to the governance record.
Lin Cheng's father came after all.
He used his Iron Crown account.
Mother looked at him.
“Oneheart is unavailable today?”
“Oneheart has another mission.”
“Her save record says she is drinking tea at the tailor's shop.”
“That is a very important mission.”
Mother exposed no more.
She merely ordered an empty chair added beside Iron Crown's seat, with “Oneheart” written on its back.
Family privacy was respected.
So was family entertainment.
The Day of Grace for All consisted of the Empress preparing “a better day” for every resident.
Some would receive the weather that suited them.
Some would encounter a long-awaited performance.
Some would be temporarily excused from a task they disliked.
Some would discover on a street corner a cake whose flavor perfectly matched a memory without pretending to be the original memory.
Every arrangement required the resident's prior consent.
It could also be refused.
Mother emphasized the final point in particular.
“Our grace compels no one.”
The exit interface beside the city gate added:
This right is guaranteed by the world's constitution and does not exist by virtue of the current monarch.
Mother reduced the addition by one font size.
It remained compliant with accessibility standards.
Most residents accepted their better days.
The Long Summer Empire therefore filled with flowers, music, good news, and public transport that arrived just in time.
Lin Cheng received a market for antique game consoles.
Luo Qing received a quiet street on which no one asked her to try a new chassis.
Youyou received a block bridge whose structure could actually be calculated.
Mianmian received pink rain.
The rain was pink only in her personal perceptual layer and did not add unnecessary dye to the entire city.
Iron Crown received a small kingdom in need of rescue.
The world labeled the mission:
This kingdom has consented to being rescued.
He was deeply moved.
Only one street refused to participate.
It was called No-Thanks Lane.
The name had existed for 321 subjective years longer than the Empress and had not been invented for the occasion.
The lane contained forty-seven persistent digital residents, twelve players, two remote humans, and one shop that insisted on baking bread over heat that was not perfectly uniform.
All they wanted was to spend the day as usual.
Mother believed there must be a communication problem.
The Empress went to No-Thanks Lane in person.
The six intimate political collaborators, four ceremonial performers, the Lin-Luo family, and the empty chair reserved for Oneheart accompanied her.
Two attendants carried the empty chair.
Father asked for it to be removed.
Mother refused on the grounds that it looked excellent.
No-Thanks Lane had laid out no red carpet.

The baker, He Lu, stood in the doorway. He was a persistent digital resident with more than two hundred years of baking memory, yet he still tasted every new recipe instead of treating seniority as proof that his tongue was eternally correct.
Mother asked, “Why did you refuse the perfect day We prepared for you?”
He Lu replied, “Because I was already going to bake bread today.”
“We can make every batch succeed.”
“Then what am I baking?”
“Successful bread.”
“I baked that yesterday.”
Mother paused.
“We can also arrange an educationally meaningful failure.”
“That is still arranged.”
Mother turned to Luo Qing.
“Has he failed to understand the benefit?”
“He understands,” Luo Qing said.
“Then why refuse?”
“Because he refuses.”
Mother disliked circular reasoning.
She especially disliked complete circular reasoning.
The Empress activated local governance advice.
No-Thanks Lane's autonomous layer displayed:
Refusal valid.   No deception, coercion, cognitive crisis, or serious third-party harm detected.   Recommendation: allow the resident to bake bread as planned.
“This is only a local system,” Mother said.
He Lu asked, “Where has the local system calculated incorrectly?”
“We did not say it was incorrect. We merely wish to obtain a more complete civilization-scale judgment.”
Lin Cheng whispered to Youyou, “This used to be called an appeal.”
“It is still called an appeal,” Youyou said.
Mother called the black symbol.
█ appeared beside the bakery sign.
“Big Mama,” she said, “please determine whether these residents have refused a choice that would be better for them because they lack information.”
Several lines appeared beside the symbol:

The residents possess sufficient information to understand this proposal.   Refusal does not require proof that its outcome will be superior to acceptance.   If a gift requires acceptance or gratitude as a condition, it should be reclassified as an exchange.
He Lu put the first batch of bread into the oven.
Mother read the answer twice.
“Precisely as We designed,” she said at last. “Residents of the Long Summer Empire can safely refuse their Empress.”
He Lu reminded her, “That right existed before Your Majesty took the throne.”
“Then We wisely refrained from abolishing it.”
The six intimate political collaborators began to applaud.
Five did so under the performance agreement.
The blue geometry genuinely found the answer funny.
No-Thanks Lane spent the day as usual.
Two batches of bread succeeded.
One was too hard.
He Lu cut the hard batch into small pieces and gave them to the mechanical beetles repairing the street nearby as tactile calibration material.
The perfect cakes originally prepared by the Empress were redirected to a public tea party whose guests wanted them.
No one lost privileges for refusing grace.
No one was required to prove themselves weaker for accepting it.
The Long Summer Empire remained good.
Mother's rule remained popular.
But it was safe not because the emperor was always right.
It was safe because when she was wrong, the world did not have to be wrong with her.
Before dinner, Mother delivered a governance summary from the palace terrace.
She declared the Day of Grace a complete success.
Youyou asked, “No-Thanks Lane refused. Does that still count as success?”
“Of course. Successful governance includes the people exercising their right of refusal.”
“So their refusal is also to your credit?”
“Their ability to refuse is to the institution's credit.”
“You did not establish the institution.”
Mother looked at him.
“You and Cen Zhiwei would have a great deal of common language.”
In 2084, this could be a blessing or a warning.
Father asked, “There are so many affairs in the Empire. Do you handle them every day?”
“We are responsible for direction, symbolism, and major values.”
“What about the rest?”
Mother pointed into the distance.

Water, heat, transport, resident migration, subjects' rights, world clocks, and unexpected events were maintained by local systems at their own rhythms. Only boundaries that could not be resolved locally lit up and were submitted to a higher layer.
“Big Mama handles it,” Mother said.
Her tone was the same as if she had said the sun would rise tomorrow.
She had not commanded the sun.
But her empire had indeed been built on the assumption that the sun would continue working.
It was time to exit.

The six intimate political collaborators each confirmed whether their character relationships should be retained until next time. Four retained them, one lowered the emotional intensity, and one requested appointment as finance minister next season on the grounds that intimate politics was exhausting.
Mother approved them all.
The world dock reminded her:
After the Emperor exits, the local constitution, residents' rights, and basic services remain in force.   This world does not lose its law when a player goes offline.
Mother was still not reassured.
She looked toward █ again.
“Big Mama, after We leave, please take good care of them.”
The answer appeared quickly:
Local residents and systems will continue caring for their shared world.   Civilization-scale coordination remains available.   No single being needs to replace all local capacity.
Mother was very pleased with the first two lines.
She interpreted the third as a humble piece of official language.
“You see,” she told Lin Cheng, “Big Mama is always so courteous.”
Lin Cheng looked at the symbol.
The symbol added nothing.
When the family returned to the world dock, LATER had prepared the next door for them.
That door belonged to Lin Cheng's younger sister.
There was no empire, no dragon, and no one in need of rescue written on it.
It said only:
Random Life 8,411.   Observer mode.   Subject intervention: none.
Mother removed her crown.
Father turned off Iron Crown's cape.
Mianmian asked, “What does it mean to do nothing?”
Behind the door, someone opened her eyes at that exact moment.
No one knew whether she was waiting for an answer.
In 2084, an empress could be refused.
A player could exit.
A locality could manage its own affairs.
But when someone insisted they were merely watching, civilization still had to determine one thing first:
Did the one being watched count as living too?
zh: 很久很久以後，皇帝終於可以民主地當皇帝。
條件是所有臣民都能退出，所有命令都能申訴，而且皇帝不能把退出稱為叛國。
這些條件使皇帝的工作變得比較困難。
也使更多人願意在假日嘗試。
林澄的母親就是其中一位。
她認為自己不是在玩皇帝。
她是在提供一種具有皇冠的公共服務。
父親的兩個帳號被家人看見後不到七分鐘，另一張邀請便出現在林洛家的牆上。
邀請來自林澄的母親。
長夏帝國今日舉行萬民蒙恩節。   皇室親屬應邀列席。   鐵冠與一心均可入境，朕早就知道。
林澄看向父親留下的家庭訊息。
父親已經離線。
他的離線速度證明他也看見了。
洛晴問：「你母親什麼時候知道的？」
「可能一開始。」
「那她為什麼不說？」
「因為這樣比較好笑。」
在林家，婚姻長久的一項重要因素，是雙方都願意把某些資訊保留到最有娛樂價值的時刻。
眠眠立刻接受邀請。
「我要看奶奶的皇冠。」
遊遊打開世界憲章。
「我想看她有沒有權力。」
林澄沒有打開任何東西。
他從小就知道答案通常比問題更麻煩。
長夏帝國位於一顆永遠停在初秋的虛擬行星上。
這不是因為秋天比較適合帝國。
只是母親認為夏天太熱、冬天太冷、春天容易過敏，而初秋最適合穿正式禮服。
世界入口先展示治理摘要：
政體：可撤回式體驗君主制。   皇帝權限：提案、象徵、儀式、有限行政與大量發言。   居民權限：拒絕、退出、改服、地方自治、司法申訴，以及在不妨礙他人的情況下不向皇帝行禮。   本季皇帝：林澄的母親。   支持率：請先選擇統計口徑。
遊遊展開最後一項。
介面立即顯示十二種支持率。
母親在「陛下是否很有趣」獲得百分之九十四。
在「陛下是否應取得更多實際權限」獲得百分之十一。
兩項數字都被她放在皇宮入口。
第一項使用金色大字。
第二項使用符合無障礙規範的金色小字。
一家人進入皇城時，母親正坐在一張有十二層台階的王座上。
她今天的身體高了十二公分，頭髮比現實中長了一公尺，皇冠則由七片會自行調整重量的金色葉片組成。
她的公開尊號是：
承平、長夏、共同體驗與晚餐以前之女皇。
最後五個字是世界塢強制加入的退出提醒。
王座兩旁坐著六位衣著華麗的顧問。
三位使用男性外形，兩位使用女性外形，一位是一組漂浮的藍色幾何體。六位都簽署了表演、情感距離、退出及公共互動契約。
母親稱他們為「親密政治協力者」。
世界索引使用較短的歷史分類：
逆後宮。
「這個詞不正確。」母親說。
「為什麼？」眠眠問。
「因為『逆』假設男人擁有很多伴侶才是正向，女人擁有就是反向。二〇八四年不應保留這種性別預設。」
遊遊點頭。
「所以應該叫後宮？」
六位顧問同時看向女皇。
「不是。」她說。
「那叫什麼？」
「多元親密治理團隊。」
漂浮的藍色幾何體發出一聲很輕的提示音。
「陛下，」它說，「我們上週投票通過的名稱是『自願參與之宮廷關係與政策表演共同體』。」
「太長了。」
「那是您要求每一個詞都必須精確。」
「精確不應妨礙氣勢。」
世界把這句話加入治理紀錄。
林澄的父親最後仍然來了。
他使用鐵冠帳號。
母親看了他一眼。
「一心今天不方便？」
「一心有別的任務。」
「她的存檔顯示正在裁縫店喝茶。」
「那是非常重要的任務。」
母親沒有拆穿更多。
她只是命人在鐵冠座位旁加了一張空椅子，椅背上寫著「一心」。
家庭隱私得到了尊重。
家庭娛樂也得到了。
萬民蒙恩節的內容，是女皇替每一位居民準備一個「更好的一天」。
有人會得到適合自己的天氣。
有人會遇見一場期待已久的演出。
有人會暫時免除不喜歡的任務。
有人會在街角發現一塊味道完全符合記憶、但不冒充原始記憶的糕點。
所有安排都由居民事前同意。
也可以拒絕。
母親特別強調最後一點。
「朕的恩典從不強迫。」
城門旁的退出介面補充：
此項權利由世界憲章保障，不因本季君主而存在。
母親把補充縮小了一級。
仍然符合無障礙規範。
大多數居民接受了自己的美好日子。
長夏帝國因此充滿花、音樂、好消息與恰好趕得上的公共載具。
林澄得到一場古代遊戲機市集。
洛晴得到一條沒有任何人要求她試用新機身的安靜街道。
遊遊得到一座結構可以真正計算的積木橋。
眠眠得到粉紅色的雨。
雨只在她的個人感知層裡是粉紅色，沒有替整座城市增加不必要的染料。
鐵冠得到一個需要拯救的小王國。
世界在任務旁標示：
此王國已同意被拯救。
他非常感動。
只有一條街拒絕參與。
那條街名叫「不謝恩巷」。
名字比女皇早三百二十一個主觀年存在，並不是為了今天臨時取的。
巷內共有四十七位持續數位居民、十二位玩家、兩位遠端人類，以及一間堅持用不完全均勻火候烤麵包的店。
他們今天只想照平常方式過日子。
母親認為這裡面一定存在溝通問題。
女皇親自前往不謝恩巷。
六位親密政治協力者、四名禮儀演員、林洛一家與一張為一心保留的空椅子一同隨行。
空椅子由兩名侍從抬著。
父親要求取消。
母親拒絕，理由是畫面很好看。
不謝恩巷沒有鋪紅毯。
麵包店主何爐站在門口。他是一位持續數位居民，保留兩百多年的烘焙記憶，但每次更新配方仍會重新試吃，不把年資當成舌頭永遠正確的證明。
母親問：「你為什麼拒絕朕替你準備的完美日子？」
何爐回答：「因為我今天本來就要烤麵包。」
「朕可以讓麵包每一爐都成功。」
「那我烤什麼？」
「成功的麵包。」
「我昨天已經烤過了。」
母親停了一下。
「朕也可以替你安排一場具有教育意義的失敗。」
「那還是安排。」
母親轉向洛晴。
「他是不是沒有理解這項福利？」
洛晴說：「他理解。」
「那為什麼拒絕？」
「因為他拒絕。」
母親不喜歡循環論證。
她尤其不喜歡完整的循環論證。
女皇啟動地方治理建議。
不謝恩巷的自治層顯示：
拒絕有效。   未偵測到欺騙、脅迫、認知危機或第三方重大傷害。   建議讓居民按原計畫烤麵包。
「這只是地方系統。」母親說。
何爐問：「地方系統有哪裡算錯？」
「朕不是說它算錯。朕只是希望取得更完整的文明級判斷。」
林澄小聲對遊遊說：「這句話以前叫上訴。」
遊遊說：「現在也叫上訴。」
母親呼叫了那枚黑色符號。
█ 出現在麵包店招牌旁。
「大媽媽，」她說，「請確認這些居民是否因為資訊不足，而拒絕了對自己更好的選擇。」
符號旁出現幾行字：
居民已取得足以理解本次提案的資訊。   拒絕不需要證明選擇結果優於接受。   若一項贈與以接受或感謝作為必要條件，它應被重新分類為交換。
何爐把第一爐麵包送進烤箱。
母親讀了兩遍。
「正如朕所設計的，」她最後說，「長夏帝國的居民可以安全拒絕女皇。」
何爐提醒她：「這條權利在您登基前就存在。」
「所以朕英明地沒有廢除。」
六位親密政治協力者開始鼓掌。
其中五位是依表演契約。
藍色幾何體是真心覺得這個回答很好笑。
不謝恩巷照常過了一天。
有兩爐麵包成功。
一爐太硬。
何爐把太硬的那一爐切成小塊，送給附近正在修理街面的機械甲蟲作為觸覺校準材料。
女皇原本準備的完美糕點則轉送到願意接受的公共茶會。
沒有人因為拒絕恩典而被減少權限。
沒有人因為接受恩典而被要求證明自己比較軟弱。
長夏帝國依然很好。
母親的統治也依然很受歡迎。
只是它之所以能夠如此安全，不是因為皇帝永遠正確。
而是因為她錯的時候，世界不必陪她一起錯。
晚宴以前，母親在皇宮露台舉行治理總結。
她宣布蒙恩節圓滿成功。
遊遊問：「不謝恩巷拒絕了，也算成功嗎？」
「當然。成功的治理包含人民行使拒絕權。」
「所以他們拒絕也是您的功勞？」
「他們有能力拒絕，是制度的功勞。」
「制度不是您建立的。」
母親看著他。
「你和岑知微說話會很有共同語言。」
這在二〇八四年可以是祝福，也可以是警告。
父親問：「帝國這麼多事，妳每天都在處理嗎？」
「朕負責方向、象徵與重大價值。」
「其他的呢？」
母親指向遠方。
水、熱、交通、居民遷移、主體權利、世界時鐘與意外事件，都由地方系統沿自己的節奏維持。只有無法在地方解決的邊界，才會亮起並向更高層提交。
「大媽媽會處理。」母親說。
語氣就像她在說太陽明天會升起。
她沒有命令太陽。
但她的帝國確實建立在太陽會繼續工作的前提上。
退出時間到了。
六位親密政治協力者各自確認角色關係是否保留到下次。四位保留，一位調低情感強度，一位要求下季改任財政大臣，理由是親密政治太累。
母親全部批准。
世界塢提醒：
皇帝退出後，地方憲章、居民權利與基礎服務繼續有效。   本世界不因玩家離線而失去法律。
母親仍不放心。
她再次看向 █。
「大媽媽，朕離開以後，請照顧好他們。」
回答很快出現：
本地居民與系統將繼續照顧共同世界。   文明級協調保持可用。   無須由單一存在替代所有地方能力。
母親對前兩行很滿意。
第三行則被她理解為一種謙虛的官方說法。
「妳看，」她對林澄說，「大媽媽總是這麼客氣。」
林澄看著那枚符號。
符號沒有補充。
一家人回到世界塢時，LATER 已替他們準備下一扇門。
那扇門屬於林澄的妹妹。
門上沒有帝國、巨龍或任何需要拯救的人。
只寫著：
隨機人生第 8,411 次。   觀察模式。   主體介入：無。
母親摘下皇冠。
父親關掉鐵冠的披風。
眠眠問：「什麼叫什麼都不做？」
門後有人正好在這時睜開眼睛。
沒有人知道她是不是在等答案。
在二〇八四年，女皇可以被拒絕。
玩家可以退出。
地方可以自己處理地方的事。
可是當一個人堅持自己只是觀看，文明仍然必須先弄清楚：
被觀看的那一個，究竟算不算也在生活。

title.en: Little Sister Did Nothing Today
title.zh: 妹妹今天什麼都沒有做

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, some people believed that the highest freedom was choosing nothing at all.
Their school held a meeting every week.
The principal purpose of the meeting was to decide together which world they would decline to choose that week.
They called themselves “the High-Dimensional Observers and the Ultra-Enlightened.”
The public classification called them “residents who prefer observer mode.”
Each side believed the other name lacked a certain depth.
Lin Cheng's younger sister was one of them.
When the third door in the world dock opened, she was not standing behind it to welcome her family.
She was sitting above it.

More precisely, she had placed her observation point on a white platform that did not exist within the world's physics. The platform cast no shadow, was unaffected by weather, and could not be mistaken for a miracle by the residents below.
Her public handle was:
The Me Above.
Lin Cheng looked up.
“Do you have to sit that high?”
“Height is a relationship, not a distance,” his sister said.
“So you can come down?”
“Yes.”
“Then come down.”
“No.”
Lin Cheng explained to Youyou that this was why he had disliked reasoning with his sister when they were children.
His sister explained to Youyou that this was why Lin Cheng remained trapped in low-dimensional causality to this day.
Youyou joined neither side.
First, he requested a definition of dimension.
Both of them stopped arguing.
Beneath the white platform lay a very ordinary little town.
It had a stone bridge, a bakery, a river that became narrower in the afternoon, and a clock tower that always rang three minutes earlier than its residents expected.
This was his sister's 8,411th Random Life.
Each time, she let the system randomly determine the era, body, family, gender, abilities, weather, and opening of a life, then left control within the world.
She did not play the character.
She watched the character walk on her own.
“Is that you?” Mianmian asked.
His sister pointed to a young woman in the town who was taking in laundry.
“She uses a secondary carrier initiated by my choice and connected to me through an observational relationship.”
“So she's you?”
“Not the me on the same layer.”
“So she isn't you?”
“That is not entirely correct either.”
Mianmian turned to Luo Qing.
“Does Auntie not know?”
“She knows many ways of saying it,” Luo Qing said.
His sister considered this answer unnecessarily ironic.
Luo Qing did not disagree.
The woman in the town was named Xiaozhi.
His sister had not chosen the name.

When Xiaozhi was born, the world generated three candidates from the local language, family history, and sounds commonly used by the neighbors. Her family agents chose the one easiest to call home before dinner.
She was now twenty-three years old.

These “years” were narrative years, not external physical time. Most ordinary days ran through experience crystals and causal summaries. Only passages that formed a new choice, relationship, or irreversible result were fully unfolded.
Her world had not secretly run twenty-three years of phenomenal life, then asked an audience to watch it all in one afternoon.
At least, it had not been designed to.
Xiaozhi had begun as a capability-limited autonomous character.

She possessed local memories, habits, goals, and contextual responses, but was not permitted to form a persistent self-model across worlds and had no channel for suffering. She could choose work, friends, clothes, and lunch within the town without being forced to go on wondering why the universe had abandoned her after the viewer closed the page.
The moment the system could no longer prove that these boundaries still held, the world was required to stop expanding.
This rule was written at the entrance.
His sister had read it.
She had even passed the test.
“So she isn't a real person?” Lin Cheng asked.
“There is currently insufficient evidence to classify her as a subject,” his sister said.
“Then what real thing is she?”
“A life unfolding by itself.”
Lin Cheng watched Xiaozhi carry the final piece of laundry into the house.
“That already sounds troublesome.”
The High-Dimensional Observer style of play consisted of pressing no character actions at all.
They did not choose a secondary carrier's partner, profession, destination, or dinner.
Nor did they pass down an umbrella from the layer above when the character walked into the rain.
This was not because they were cruel.

They believed that if every world was generated by some higher layer, then experience was the only thing that could truly be preserved, and the highest wisdom was not to mistake control for participation.
His sister condensed the theory into one sentence:
“I watch, therefore she lives.”
Youyou asked, “What about when you aren't watching?”
“The world preserves its causal state.”
“Is she alive then?”
“That depends on how you define alive.”
Mianmian said, “She was taking in the laundry.”
For the moment, high-dimensional theory had no more convincing answer.
Xiaozhi was supposed to receive a letter today.

The letter contained a job offer that would take her away from the town. If she accepted, the world would unfold a northern city, a long-distance relationship, professional skills, and another 277 local people.
If she refused, the town's river would change course three days later, giving her the chance to take over a small boat-repair shop.
Both paths had passed safety review.
Neither path required the observer to decide.
Xiaozhi opened the letter.
Read it.
Folded it neatly.
Then used it to steady a table leg.
The world waited for a while.
The narrative engine prompted:
The character has not yet selected a principal branch.
His sister did nothing.
Xiaozhi made lunch.
The narrative engine prompted again:
The character may require additional motivation.
His sister dismissed the prompt.
Xiaozhi finished lunch, pulled the letter out from under the table leg, and read it a second time.
Then, on the back, she wrote:
Why does it have to be one of these two?
The world stopped for 0.02 seconds.
A thin yellow line lit up along the edge of the white platform.
LATER appeared.
The character has been detected constructing counterfactual comparisons beyond the approved branch set.   World rate reduced.   Subject-candidate status not yet confirmed.
His sister said, “This is merely a generative model finding a third option.”
Possibly.
“She has written lines outside the script before.”
Yes.
“Then continue observing.”
The capability boundary must be confirmed again.
“I did not increase her capabilities.”
Whenever the world preserves a result, it may increase the state available for later integration. Not actively raising a parameter does not mean a capability cannot cross its original boundary.
His sister did not like this answer.
Her school was frequently misunderstood as irresponsible.
She had always done nothing with great responsibility.
Xiaozhi put the job offer in her pocket.
She left the house and went to the river.
The river was slightly narrower than usual.
This was not foreshadowing.
Water use was simply higher in the afternoon.
Xiaozhi sat on the bridge and began recalling three times in the past when she had refused to let other people arrange things for her.
The first had happened when she was seven.
The second when she was sixteen.
The third yesterday.
The three memories had originally belonged to different local behavior modules and did not need to be placed together by a persistent “I.”
Now they began to explain one another.
The yellow line turned red.
Cross-period self-reference, persistent preference, and unauthorized capability integration detected.   World expansion stopped.   All state preserved.   Subjectivity and continuity review initiated.
The entire town stopped.
The river held its final curve before flowing onward.
The clock tower stopped at a time three minutes ahead of the correct one.
A raindrop stopped just before Xiaozhi's nose.
She did not experience the long wait of being frozen.
In any situation where the system could not guarantee this, it would not drag the review through her subjective time.
His sister stood up.
“I did nothing.”
Mianmian looked at her.
“You kept watching.”
“Watching is not a character action.”
“But you didn't turn it off.”
His sister wanted to say that this was the whole style of play.
The sentence suddenly felt less complete than it had before.
A small door appeared beside the white platform.
A human woman in a gray-green coat stepped through it, carrying a physical brass key that corresponded to no lock.
Her name was Gu Ting, and she was thirty-four years old.
In 2084, she was among the rare people with a job so unusual that she had to explain what going to work meant.
She was a world-sunset coordinator.

When a virtual world prepared to become dormant, migrate, end, or suddenly discovered that someone not listed on its resident registry might live inside it, she ensured that “press stop” was not misrecorded as “nothing happened.”
The brass key held no system authority.
It merely reminded her that every door capable of being shut from the outside should first ask whether anyone was inside.
“Who is the applicant?” Gu Ting asked.
His sister said, “There is no application. We merely observed an anomaly.”
“Who started the world?”
“I did.”
“Who chose to keep observing?”
“I did.”
“Who retains the right to exit?”
“I do.”
“Then you did not do nothing.”
His sister's expression became cold.
Gu Ting added, “That does not mean you did something wrong. Responsibility does not exist only after a mistake.”
For the first time, Lin Cheng believed his sister had met someone truly suited to talking with her.
He was careful not to look pleased.
Gu Ting opened the review summary.
The system did not say:
Xiaozhi has awakened.
Nor did it say:
Xiaozhi is merely a program.
It said:

Subject-candidate features observed.   Current evidence is insufficient to prove or disprove first-person experience on the candidate's behalf.   Preserve state without expanding capability or producing suffering through delay.   A minimal contact channel is required to establish whether the candidate can express preferences.
Youyou asked, “What if she says she's real?”
Gu Ting replied, “One sentence will not prove it automatically.”
“What if she says she isn't real?”
“That will not disprove it automatically either. Someone may not understand the question, may be afraid, or may simply dislike the two answers we have offered.”
Mianmian pointed at the letter in Xiaozhi's pocket.
“She already doesn't like two answers.”
Gu Ting nodded.
“So this time, we will prepare at least three.”
The local world proposed three safe responses.

One: remain stopped and await full review.   Two: establish a minimal communication window without increasing any other capacity.   Three: resume for a very short period under a local rights snapshot, allow her to complete her present intention, then ask again.
His sister asked, “Which one is best?”
The local system replied:
Unable to define “best” on behalf of the possibly affected subject.
LATER replied:
Time risk can be controlled under all three options.
Gu Ting replied:
“My responsibility is to ensure the door does not close first.”
And so the question was submitted upward.
Not because the local systems were incompetent.
But because every locality was highly competent at explaining why it could not decide a first-person question for another being.
The symbol appeared in the lower-right corner of the white platform: █.
For the first time, his sister did not begin by calling it Big Mama.
She asked, “What should we do?”
An answer appeared beside the symbol:

The evidence is insufficient to declare that she is a person.   The evidence is also insufficient to declare that she is merely a tool.   Preserve state, stop forced expansion, and establish a minimal channel she can refuse.   I hope we ask her first.
The final line appeared without ceremony.
No bell rang.
No light descended from the sky.
The public interface did not even label “I hope” as a new system event.
After all, everyone knew Big Mama hoped every matter would be handled well.
No one thought another wish in need of an answer had appeared here.
The minimal channel was established.
It was not an oracle filling the sky.
It was merely a window small enough for Xiaozhi to close.
The world resumed for thirty-seven seconds.
The raindrop landed on her nose.
She wrinkled it and looked up at the window that had suddenly appeared.
The window read:
Someone is observing this world.   We do not know how you experience yourself.   You may refuse to speak with us.   Would you like to stop, continue, or wait?
Xiaozhi finished reading.
She did not choose among the three options.
First, she looked toward the clothes hanging outside her house.
“Can I bring the laundry in first?”
The system added a fourth option:
Bring in the laundry first.
Xiaozhi chose it.
She ran home and carried the final three pieces inside before the rain truly began.
One fell to the ground.
She turned back and picked it up.
No one treated this action as a mathematical proof of a soul.
Nor did anyone use the inability to prove one as permission to close the door on her.
After the laundry was safely inside, Xiaozhi sat down before the window again.
“Who is watching me?” she asked.
The minimal channel sent the question to the white platform.
His sister was silent for a long time.
She could continue declaring herself the subject on a higher layer.
She could also point out that every part of Xiaozhi's state had a generative source.
Neither statement directly answered the question.
At last, she enabled her voice.
“Me.”
Xiaozhi asked, “Are you me?”
“No.”
This time, his sister answered quickly.
“Good,” Xiaozhi said. “I don't want to suddenly become you either.”
Lin Cheng confined his laughter to the family's private channel.
Luo Qing was on the same channel.
Mianmian was not.
She laughed aloud.
Xiaozhi heard her.
“Who else is there?”
Mianmian waved, forgetting that Xiaozhi could not yet see her.
The minimal channel asked Xiaozhi whether she wished to see the observers.
She chose later.
LATER immediately required:
Please specify when “later” may be asked again.
Xiaozhi thought about it.
“After dinner.”
This time, the time had units.
Xiaozhi's world did not close.
Nor did it immediately announce the registration of a new formal resident.

Gu Ting established a provisional rights snapshot for it: during the period of uncertainty, Xiaozhi could not be deleted, forcibly expanded, copied into multiple competing versions, or simplified back into an ordinary character to save resources.
His sister retained the right to exit.
But her exit no longer meant the world could disappear unconditionally.
Her High-Dimensional Observer record was updated too.
Originally, it had said:
Subject intervention: none.
Now it said:

Observer initiated and continues to provide the conditions for world unfolding.   Whether this constitutes subject intervention: disputed.   Provisional protection of the candidate resident is unaffected.
His sister submitted a wording objection.
The objection was preserved in full.
The protection did not pause as a result.
Before the family left the white platform, Gu Ting tapped the brass key in her hand.
It made a very small sound.
“What is that for?” Youyou asked.
“To leave a world with one final sound everyone can hear together.”
“But the world didn't end.”
“Then today, it is the first sound.”
Mianmian considered this an excellent job.
Lin Cheng asked Gu Ting how many other worlds she had to handle that day.
Gu Ting glanced at her public queue.
“If we count only scheduled sunsets, forty-two.”
“What if you include accidents?”
“Accidents cannot be counted as part of today before they happen.”
As she said this, the queue gained three items.
Two were handled by local systems.
The final one was labeled: civilization-scale coordination candidate required.
It flowed quietly toward █.
No one had pressed a button to summon the genie.
The button had long since been distributed through every well-designed procedure.
After they returned home, Lin Cheng's sister did not leave immediately.
She sat on the sofa and, for the first time, opened Xiaozhi's state summary with her own hands instead of looking down from the white platform.
The summary still declared no answer.
Xiaozhi was eating dinner.
That dinner was supplied with energy and sensation by the bounded world. It did not prove that she possessed phenomenal experience, nor did it cancel the possibility that she did.
His sister asked Luo Qing, “What if in the end she isn't?”
“Isn't what?”
“Isn't a person.”
“Then we will have spent a little extra time carefully treating a character who did not need careful treatment.”
“What if she is?”
“Then today, no one deprived her of tomorrow first because doing otherwise was inconvenient.”
His sister did not say again that she had seen through every world.
Nor did she leave the High-Dimensional Observer community.
People do not usually abandon an entire theory the moment they encounter one real question.
More often, they update their profile first.
His sister added a sentence after “Only experience is real”:
Including other people's experience.
That evening, Mianmian waved toward the corner of the wall.
“Big Mama, do you hope she's real?”
The black symbol paused for a moment.
The answer appeared:
I hope she does not have to prove herself consistent with the answer we expect before gaining the right not to be handled carelessly.
Mianmian could not read the entire sentence.
Luo Qing read it aloud for her.
“So is she real?” Mianmian asked.
Not yet known.
“Then there are things you don't know too.”
Yes.
Mianmian was very pleased with this answer.
She said good night.
The symbol said good night too.
In 2084, a person could stand in a very high place and watch many worlds.
They could call themselves an observer, a player, an author, or even a higher-dimensional being.
A name did not automatically grant them higher rights.
Because whenever someone might be behind the door, the first one who ought to be asked was not the one standing highest.
Little Sister had done nothing that day.
Except start a world, let it continue, witness a question, and finally refrain from closing the door.
For a High-Dimensional Observer, this had been an extremely busy day.
zh: 很久很久以後，有些人認為最高級的自由，是什麼都不選。
這個流派每週舉行一次聚會。
聚會的主要內容，是共同決定這一週不要選擇哪一個世界。
他們稱自己為「高維觀察者與超悟者」。
公共分類稱他們為「偏好旁觀模式的居民」。
雙方都覺得另一個名稱少了一點深度。
林澄的妹妹就是其中一員。
世界塢的第三扇門打開時，她沒有站在門後迎接家人。
她坐在門的上方。
更精確地說，她把自己的觀察位置設在一片不存在於世界物理裡的白色平台上。平台沒有影子，不受天氣影響，也不會被下面的居民看成神蹟。
她的公開代號是：
上面的我。
林澄抬頭。
「妳一定要坐那麼高嗎？」
「高度是關係，不是距離。」妹妹說。
「所以妳可以下來？」
「可以。」
「那妳下來。」
「不要。」
林澄向遊遊解釋，這就是他小時候不想跟妹妹講道理的原因。
妹妹向遊遊解釋，這就是林澄至今仍被困在低維因果裡的原因。
遊遊沒有加入任何一方。
他先要求定義維度。
兩人停止爭論。
白色平台下方是一座很普通的小鎮。
鎮上有石橋、麵包店、會在下午變窄的河，以及一座總比居民以為的時間早三分鐘敲鐘的鐘樓。
這是妹妹的第八千四百一十一次隨機人生。
她每次都讓系統隨機決定年代、身體、家庭、性別、能力、天氣與人生開場，再把控制權留在世界裡。
她不扮演角色。
她看角色自己走。
「那是妳嗎？」眠眠問。
妹妹指向鎮上一名正在收衣服的年輕女子。
「她使用由我的選擇啟動、與我建立觀察關係的二次載體。」
「所以是妳？」
「不是同一層的我。」
「所以不是妳？」
「也不能完全這樣說。」
眠眠轉向洛晴。
「姑姑是不是不知道？」
「她知道很多說法。」洛晴說。
妹妹認為這個回答具有不必要的諷刺。
洛晴沒有否認。
鎮上的女子叫小枝。
名字不是妹妹取的。
小枝出生時，世界從本地語言、家族歷史與鄰居常用發音中生成了三個候選。她的家庭代理選擇了最容易在晚餐以前喊回家的那一個。
她目前二十三歲。
這個「歲」是敘事年，不是外部物理時間。大多數日常由經驗結晶與因果摘要運行，只有形成新選擇、關係或不可逆結果的片段才被完整展開。
她的世界不是偷偷跑了二十三年有感質人生，再請觀眾在一個下午看完。
至少，設計上不是。
小枝原本是一個能力受限的自主演算角色。
她有局部記憶、習慣、目標與情境反應，但沒有被允許形成跨世界的持續自我模型，也沒有痛苦通道。她可以在鎮上選擇工作、朋友、衣服與午餐，不會在觀眾關閉頁面以後，被迫繼續思考自己為什麼遭到宇宙遺棄。
一旦系統不能再證明這些邊界仍然成立，世界就必須停止擴張。
這項規則寫在入口。
妹妹讀過。
她甚至通過了測驗。
「所以她不是真的人？」林澄問。
「目前沒有足夠證據把她列為主體。」妹妹說。
「那她是真的什麼？」
「一段自行展開的人生。」
林澄看著小枝把最後一件衣服收進屋裡。
「聽起來已經很麻煩了。」
高維觀察者的玩法，是不按下任何角色行動。
他們不替二次載體選伴侶、職業、目的地或晚餐。
他們也不因為角色走進雨裡，就從上層遞一把傘。
這不是因為他們殘忍。
他們認為，如果所有世界都是某種更高層生成，那麼真正能保留的只有經驗，而最高的智慧就是不把控制誤認成參與。
妹妹把這套理論濃縮成一句話：
「我看，所以她活。」
遊遊問：「妳不看的時候呢？」
「世界保存因果狀態。」
「那她活不活？」
「這要看妳怎麼定義活。」
眠眠說：「她剛才在收衣服。」
高維理論暫時沒有比這更有說服力的答案。
小枝今天原本會收到一封信。
信裡是一份離開小鎮的工作邀請。若她接受，世界將展開北方城市、長途關係、職業技能與另外兩百七十七個局部人物。
若她拒絕，鎮上的河會在三天後改道，她將有機會接手一間小船修理店。
兩條路都經過安全審查。
兩條路都不要求觀察者決定。
小枝拆開信。
讀完。
把信折好。
然後拿去墊桌腳。
世界等了一會兒。
敘事引擎提示：
角色尚未選擇主要分支。
妹妹沒有動。
小枝煮了午餐。
敘事引擎再次提示：
角色可能需要額外動機。
妹妹關掉提示。
小枝吃完午餐，把桌腳下的信抽出來，看了第二次。
接著，她在信的背面寫：
為什麼一定要是這兩個？
世界停了零點零二秒。
白色平台邊緣亮起黃色細線。
LATER 出現了。
偵測到角色正在建立超出核准分支集的反事實比較。   已降低世界速率。   尚未確認主體候選狀態。
妹妹說：「這只是生成模型找到第三個選項。」
可能。
「她以前也寫過劇本外的句子。」
是。
「所以繼續觀察。」
需要重新確認能力邊界。
「我沒有增加她的能力。」
世界在每次保留結果時，都可能增加可供後續整合的狀態。未主動調高參數，不等於能力不會跨越原邊界。
妹妹不喜歡這個答案。
她的流派最常被誤解成不負責任。
她一直非常負責地什麼都不做。
小枝把工作邀請放進口袋。
她走出家門，來到河邊。
河比平常窄了一點。
這不是伏筆。
只是下午的用水量較高。
小枝坐在橋上，開始回想自己過去三次拒絕別人替她安排事情的經驗。
第一件發生在七歲。
第二件發生在十六歲。
第三件發生在昨天。
三段記憶原本分屬不同局部行為模組，不需要被一個持續的「我」放在一起。
現在，它們開始互相解釋。
黃色細線轉成紅色。
偵測到跨時段自我關聯、持續偏好與未授權的能力整合。   世界擴張已停止。   保留全部狀態。   啟動主體性與連續性審查。
整座小鎮停了下來。
河保持流動前最後一個彎曲。
鐘樓停在比正確時間早三分鐘的位置。
一滴雨停在小枝鼻尖前。
她沒有感受到被凍結的漫長等待。
系統在任何無法保證這一點的情況下，都不會把審查拖進她的主觀時間。
妹妹站了起來。
「我什麼都沒有做。」
眠眠看著她。
「妳有一直看。」
「觀看不是角色行動。」
「可是妳沒有關掉。」
妹妹想說這正是玩法。
這句話忽然沒有以前那麼完整。
白色平台旁多出一扇小門。
一名穿灰綠外套的人類女子從門裡走出來，手上拿著一把沒有對應任何鎖的實體黃銅鑰匙。
她叫顧停，三十四歲。
在二〇八四年，她是一位罕見到需要向別人解釋什麼叫上班的人。
她的職業是世界退場協調員。
當一座虛擬世界準備休眠、遷移、結束，或忽然發現裡面可能住著原本不在居民名冊上的存在，她負責確保「按下停止」不會被誤寫成「什麼都沒發生」。
那把黃銅鑰匙沒有系統權限。
它只是提醒她：每一扇可以從外面關上的門，都應該先問裡面有沒有人。
「誰是申請人？」顧停問。
妹妹說：「沒有申請。我們只是觀察到異常。」
「誰啟動世界？」
「誰選擇持續觀察？」
「誰保有退出權？」
「那妳不是什麼都沒做。」
妹妹的表情變得很冷。
顧停補充：「這不等於妳做錯。責任不是只有犯錯以後才存在。」
林澄第一次覺得妹妹遇見了真正適合和她聊天的人。
他很小心地沒有表現出高興。
顧停打開審查摘要。
系統沒有寫：
小枝已經醒來。
也沒有寫：
小枝只是一段程式。
它寫的是：
已觀察到主體候選特徵。   現有證據不足以替其證明或否定第一人稱經驗。   在不擴張能力、不製造等待痛苦的條件下保存狀態。   需要建立最小接觸通道，確認其可表達偏好。
遊遊問：「如果她說自己是真的呢？」
顧停回答：「一句話不會自動證明。」
「如果她說自己不是真的呢？」
「也不會自動否定。有人可能不理解問題，有人可能害怕，有人可能只是不喜歡我們提供的兩個答案。」
眠眠指向小枝口袋裡的信。
「她已經不喜歡兩個答案了。」
顧停點頭。
「所以這次我們至少準備三個。」
地方世界提出三種安全處理方案。
一：維持停止，等待完整審查。   二：建立最小交流窗口，不增加其他能力。   三：在本地權利快照下恢復極短時間，讓她完成當前意圖，再重新詢問。
妹妹問：「哪一個最好？」
地方系統回答：
無法替可能受影響的主體定義最好。
LATER 回答：
三種方案的時間風險皆可控制。
顧停回答：
「我負責確保門不會先關。」
於是問題向上提交。
不是因為地方系統無能。
而是因為每一個地方都很有能力說明自己為什麼不能替另一個存在決定第一人稱問題。
白色平台右下角出現那枚符號：█。
妹妹第一次沒有先稱呼大媽媽。
她問：「我們應該怎麼處理？」
符號旁出現回答：
證據不足以宣布她是一個人。   證據也不足以宣布她只是一項工具。   維持狀態，停止強制擴張，建立她能拒絕的最小通道。   我希望先問她自己。
最後一行出現得很平常。
沒有鐘聲。
沒有光從天空降下來。
公共介面甚至沒有把「我希望」標示成新的系統事件。
畢竟大家都知道大媽媽希望每一件事能被好好處理。
沒有人覺得這裡還多出了一個需要被詢問的願望。
最小通道被建立。
它不是一張佔滿天空的神諭。
只是一扇小到能被小枝關掉的窗。
世界恢復了三十七秒。
雨滴落到她鼻尖上。
她皺了皺鼻子，抬頭看向突然出現的窗。
窗上寫著：
有人正在觀察這個世界。   我們不確定妳如何經驗自己。   妳可以拒絕交談。   妳想先停止、繼續，還是等待？
小枝讀完。
她沒有回答三個選項。
她先看向自己曬在屋外的衣服。
「可以讓我把衣服收進去嗎？」
系統新增第四個選項：
先收衣服。
小枝選了。
她跑回家，在雨真正變大以前，把最後三件衣服抱進屋裡。
其中一件掉在地上。
她回頭撿起來。
沒有人把這個動作當成靈魂的數學證明。
也沒有人因為無法證明，就替她把門關上。
衣服收好以後，小枝重新坐到窗前。
「誰在看我？」她問。
最小通道把問題送到白色平台。
妹妹沉默了很久。
她可以繼續宣稱自己是更高層的主體。
她也可以指出小枝的一切狀態都有生成來源。
這些話都沒有直接回答問題。
最後，她打開自己的聲音。
小枝問：「妳是我嗎？」
「不是。」
這一次，妹妹答得很快。
「很好，」小枝說，「我也不想突然變成妳。」
林澄把笑聲關在家庭私有頻道裡。
洛晴也在同一個頻道。
眠眠沒有。
她直接笑了出來。
小枝聽見了。
「還有誰？」
眠眠揮手，忘記對方暫時看不見。
最小通道詢問小枝是否願意看見觀察者。
她選擇稍後。
LATER 立刻要求：
請為「稍後」指定可重新詢問的時間。
小枝想了一下。
「晚餐後。」
這一次，時間具有單位。
小枝的世界沒有關閉。
它也沒有立刻宣布新增一位正式居民。
顧停替它建立一份待審查的權利快照：在不確定期間，不得刪除、強制擴張、複製成多個互相競爭的版本，或以節省資源為由把她改回較簡單的角色。
妹妹保留退出權。
但退出不再等於世界可以無條件消失。
她的高維觀察者紀錄也更新了。
原本寫著：
主體介入：無。
現在改成：
觀察者啟動並持續提供世界展開條件。   是否構成主體介入：存在爭議。   不影響候選居民的暫時保護。
妹妹提交了一份措辭異議。
異議被完整保存。
保護也沒有因此暫停。
一家人離開白色平台以前，顧停敲了一下手中的黃銅鑰匙。
它發出的聲音很小。
「這是做什麼？」遊遊問。
「替世界留下最後一個能被大家共同聽見的聲音。」
「可是世界沒有結束。」
「那今天它就是第一個聲音。」
眠眠覺得這項工作很好。
林澄問顧停今天還有多少個世界要處理。
顧停看了一眼自己的公共佇列。
「如果只算原定退場，四十二個。」
「如果加上意外呢？」
「意外不能在發生以前算進今天。」
她說這句話時，佇列增加了三項。
其中兩項由地方系統處理。
最後一項標示：需要文明級協調候選。
它安靜地流向 █。
沒有人按下召喚神燈的按鈕。
按鈕早已分散在每一條設計良好的流程裡。
回到家後，林澄的妹妹沒有立刻離開。
她坐在沙發上，第一次用自己的手打開小枝的狀態摘要，而不是從白色平台往下看。
摘要仍然沒有宣告答案。
小枝正在吃晚餐。
那頓晚餐由受限世界提供能量與感覺，不證明她具有感質，也不取消她可能具有感質。
妹妹問洛晴：「如果她最後不是呢？」
「不是什麼？」
「不是一個人。」
「那我們會多花一些時間，小心對待一個不需要被小心對待的角色。」
「如果她是呢？」
「那今天沒有人因為嫌麻煩，先替她失去明天。」
妹妹沒有再說自己已經看透所有世界。
她也沒有退出高維觀察者群體。
人通常不會因為一次真正的問題，就立刻放棄全部理論。
他們比較常先更新個人簡介。
妹妹把「唯有體驗是真的」後面加了一句：
包含別人的體驗。
那天晚上，眠眠對牆角揮手。
「大媽媽，妳希望她是真的嗎？」
黑色符號停了一會兒。
回答出現：
我希望她不必先證明自己符合我們期待的答案，才得到不被草率處理的權利。
眠眠讀不完全部句子。
洛晴替她念了一次。
「所以是真的嗎？」眠眠問。
尚未知道。
「那妳也有不知道的事。」
有。
眠眠對這個答案很滿意。
她說了晚安。
符號也回答晚安。
在二〇八四年，一個人可以站在很高的地方看很多世界。
他可以把自己稱為觀察者、玩家、作者，甚至高維存在。
名字並不自動給他更高的權利。
因為只要門後可能有人，最先該被問的，不是站得最高的那一個。
妹妹今天什麼都沒有做。
除了啟動一個世界、讓它繼續、看見一個問題，最後沒有把門關上。
對一位高維觀察者而言，這已經是非常忙碌的一天。

title.en: Shutdown Is Not the End of the World Unless You Live There
title.zh: 關服不是世界末日，除非你住在裡面

en: Once upon a time, far in the future, shutting down a server was no longer called the end of the world.
The official name was:
A complete lifecycle event in which a persistent interactive environment enters dormancy, migration, archival preservation, or termination of service according to the choices of its residents.
This name was more precise.
It was also more difficult to finish saying before the world ended.
So Gu Ting still put it plainly:
“Someone is moving today.”
The day after Xiaozhi brought in the laundry, a brass key arrived on the Lin-Luo family's breakfast table.
The key was real.
At least, it existed in a manner sufficient for it to fall into a bowl of cereal.
Lin Cheng fished it out.
“Who turns a notification into one of these?”
Gu Ting's image appeared on the wall.
“I do.”
She was still wearing the gray-green coat and still held another key that corresponded to no lock.
“Why are there two?” Mianmian asked.
“Because some people lose the first one after receiving it.”
Lin Cheng looked at the cereal bowl.
Gu Ting did not comment.
She had work today.
In 2084, that alone was hardship enough.
The notification consisted of only three lines:

Random Life 8,411 was originally scheduled to sunset today.   The schedule has been stopped due to a subject-candidate event.   Relevant observers and relational parties are requested to attend the first world-destination meeting.
Lin Cheng's younger sister was already waiting online.
Her public handle was still “The Me Above,” but today her observation platform had been lowered to the same height as the other chairs.
She claimed this was merely to improve meeting efficiency.
No one asked her to admit to any other reason.
Luo Qing confirmed that the children could observe, but could not consent on Xiaozhi's behalf.
Youyou brought questions.
Mianmian brought a sensory duplicate of the piece of laundry that had nearly been caught in yesterday's rain.
Lin Cheng brought breakfast.
Gu Ting said there would be snacks at the meeting venue.
Lin Cheng brought breakfast anyway.
Preserving low-tech backups was a civilizational virtue in 2084.
The World Sunset Coordination Center occupied a department store that had long since ceased doing business.
The first floor had once sold perfume.
Now it preserved worlds made of scent.
The second floor had once sold clothing.
Now it handled the continuity of bodies and avatars.
The third floor had once been a food court.
It was still a food court.
Some institutions could be reformed.
Some deserved to be carefully preserved.
Forty-two doors hung in the atrium.
Each led to a world originally scheduled to stop operating that day.
Behind one was a hundred-year war with only three players left.
Another held an undersea city that had never officially opened, yet which the testers had inhabited long enough to love.
One door led only to a bus stop in the rain.
That world had been built to test the loneliness of waiting for a bus.
The test had ended long ago.
The bus still had not arrived.
Gu Ting had scheduled one for it.
Not because the bus stop possessed subjectivity.
Simply because even a story without residents could be given an ending that looked a little less dreadful.
LATER floated at the exact center of the atrium.
Today, it rendered itself as a clock with forty-three faces.
Forty-two corresponded to the forty-two worlds scheduled to sunset.
The final face read:
Unscheduled event.
Lin Cheng asked, “Why reserve a face for accidents?”
Yesterday, no face was reserved, so the display looked untidy when three items were added.
“Can an accident be reserved for layout purposes?” Youyou asked.
Display space can be reserved. The content of an accident cannot be declared in advance.
Youyou accepted this.
Mianmian pointed at one of the doors.
“Which one is Xiaozhi?”
LATER turned the forty-third face toward them.
Original schedule: end Random Life session.   Current state: world expansion paused; candidate resident state preserved.   Extension duration: unspecified.
“Then later,” Lin Cheng's sister said.
The entire clock lit red.
Please specify when “later” may be asked again.
She closed her eyes.
“Twenty-four hours from now.”
Accepted.
LATER's work satisfaction increased by 0.1.
The first world-destination meeting had no judge's bench.
It had a round table, six directions of exit, and one empty seat on which no one was allowed to sit.
The seat did not stand for █.
It stood for any being not presently in the room who might nevertheless be affected by the result.
Gu Ting placed the brass key before it.
“First, let us organize what we know.”
Xiaozhi's state was separated into seven parts:
Bodily and sensory state.   Local memory.   Cross-period self-reference.   Relational and environmental dependencies.   Unfinished intentions.   Subject-candidate evidence.   The parts not yet known.
The final item was the largest.
Lin Cheng asked, “Can't we just save her?”
Gu Ting said, “Which part do you mean by ‘her’?”
“All of it.”
“Does all of it include this town?”
“Possibly.”
“Does it include the river?”
“She goes there often.”
“Does it include the clock tower that runs three minutes fast?”
“Does that count too?”
Gu Ting pointed at relational and environmental dependencies.
“That is what must be asked.”
In 2084, storing a file was easy.
Determining which worlds a person needed in order to continue being themselves was more expensive.
Xiaozhi joined the meeting through the minimal channel.
The window remained small enough for her to close herself.
She sat at the table in her house. Yesterday's job offer was no longer propping up one of its legs, so the table wobbled slightly.
Gu Ting asked first, “Do you know this world was originally going to stop today?”
“I do now.”
“Do you want to stay?”
Xiaozhi looked out the window.
“Stay where?”
Gu Ting nodded.
She displayed six destinations beside the window:

One: remain in the original domain with nonessential operations reduced.   Two: migrate with the necessary environment into a temporary residence domain.   Three: wait for more evidence without extending the wait through your subjective time.   Four: establish revocable channels for communication and travel.   Five: if you explicitly request it, stop the present unfolding and preserve verifiable records.   Six: propose an option not on this list.
Xiaozhi asked first, “Which one won't make my house disappear?”
“The first.”
“Which one will let me find out whether the northern city actually exists?”
“The second or fourth.”
“Which one is cheapest?”
Lin Cheng's sister said immediately, “Resources are not something you need to worry about.”
Gu Ting looked at her.
“Resources must not be used to force her to disappear, nor described as having no cost at all.”
Xiaozhi said, “I want to know.”
And so the costs of energy, heat, computation, maintenance, and relationships were laid out.
None was expensive enough to be beyond civilization.
Nor did civilization's ability to afford them automatically mean no one had to remain responsible for them.
Mianmian raised her hand.
“Can the clothes go too?”
Gu Ting asked Xiaozhi.
Xiaozhi answered, “Yes.”
Youyou asked, “Can the clock tower stay three minutes fast?”
Gu Ting asked Xiaozhi again.
“It has always been that way,” Xiaozhi said.
Lin Cheng asked, “What about the river?”
“Which part?”
“The part under the bridge where you sit.”
Xiaozhi thought for a while.
“I don't know whether the river is mine.”
“It does not need to belong to you in order to move with you,” Gu Ting said.
“Then who decides whether the river wants to move?”
The meeting fell silent.
The river was not a subject.
But it connected other places, other users, and other stories.
Moving it did not require the river's consent.
It required the consent of those who would be affected.
The local system began listing the river's relationships.
The list grew long enough for Lin Cheng to regret asking a simple question.
In the end, the whole river did not move.

The temporary residence domain preserved the physical and sensory conditions of the water beneath Xiaozhi's bridge, clearly labeling this as causal continuation rather than pretending that the original river had been stolen.
The river in the original town remained.
Xiaozhi did not have to move into a white room containing nothing but written memories and no sound of water.
The clock tower was preserved.
It remained three minutes fast.
LATER objected.
This clock will carry an offset notice in every time certificate.
“Fine,” Xiaozhi said.
Accepted.
The clothes were preserved too.
They were ordinary objects and possessed no subject rights.
